items.title: OS discovery (lsb_release/dpkg-query/getconf) still runs 3x per process after #47038, twice concurrently inside Tokio polls

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: exec
labels.description: Issues related to the `codex exec` subcommand

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

`codex-cli 0.0.0` built from source at `8094365e6a2da38be1cd37d58f308c496e3f7ac9`

### What subscription do you have?

None (API key, local mock provider)

### Which model were you using?

N/A (mock Responses server; OS discovery happens before the first request)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 6.8.0-1061-aws x86_64 x86_64 (Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS)

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

N/A (non-interactive `codex exec`)

### Codex doctor report

not included: built from source with a fresh `CODEX_HOME` and no auth, so the report only shows missing credentials

### What issue are you seeing?

Since #47038 ("Cache OS discovery for user agents and telemetry"), `os_info::get()` is cached separately in three places. One `codex exec` process on Linux therefore still runs OS discovery three times: `lsb_release -a`, `dpkg-query` and `getconf LONG_BIT`, three times each. Two of those runs start at the same moment on two different Tokio worker threads. Each one runs synchronously inside an async poll, so the worker is blocked for 56–85 ms. One of the blocked tasks is the in-process app-server's `initialize` request handler.

The three caches, pinned to `8094365` (the same lines are unchanged on `main` at `e790ce2`):

- https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/8094365e6a2da38be1cd37d58f308c496e3f7ac9/codex-rs/otel/src/metrics/client.rs#L583
- https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/8094365e6a2da38be1cd37d58f308c496e3f7ac9/codex-rs/login/src/auth/default_client.rs#L155
- https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/8094365e6a2da38be1cd37d58f308c496e3f7ac9/codex-rs/analytics/src/events.rs#L1519

```rust
static OS_INFO: LazyLock<os_info::Info> = LazyLock::new(os_info::get);
```

Each `static` is a separate `LazyLock`, so each one runs `os_info::get()` the first time it is used. On Debian/Ubuntu, `lsb_release` is a Python script (`#!/usr/bin/python3 -Es`).

#### Actual behavior

Three runs on the stock build, with no local changes:

```
== run 1
lsb_release pid=66784 starts at +40ms,  runs 54ms
lsb_release pid=66800 starts at +306ms, runs 50ms
lsb_release pid=66801 starts at +306ms, runs 51ms
      3 /usr/bin/dpkg-query
      3 /usr/bin/getconf
      3 /usr/bin/lsb_release
== run 2
lsb_release pid=67622 starts at +29ms,  runs 52ms
lsb_release pid=67640 starts at +255ms, runs 59ms
lsb_release pid=67641 starts at +255ms, runs 59ms
== run 3
lsb_release pid=68431 starts at +24ms,  runs 54ms
lsb_release pid=68447 starts at +237ms, runs 52ms
lsb_release pid=68448 starts at +237ms, runs 52ms
```

(Offsets are measured from the `execve` of `codex`. Runs 2 and 3 also show 3× `dpkg-query` and 3× `getconf`.)

A gdb breakpoint on `os_info::get` (`break os_info::get` followed by `bt`) shows a different caller for each of the three hits:

```
hit 1: otel/src/metrics/client.rs:584   os_resource_attributes
       otel/src/metrics/client.rs:351
       otel/src/provider.rs:231
       core/src/otel_init.rs:85
       exec/src/lib.rs:664
hit 2: login/src/auth/default_client.rs:157   get_codex_user_agent
       login/src/auth/default_client.rs:459   default_headers
       core-plugins/src/remote.rs:179
       core-plugins/src/remote_legacy.rs:137
       core-plugins/src/manager.rs:1900
       core-plugins/src/manager.rs:2940       (tokio::spawn at manager.rs:2936)
hit 3: analytics/src/events.rs:1520     current_runtime_metadata
       analytics/src/client.rs:413      track_initialize
       app-server/src/request_processors/initialize_processor.rs:185
       app-server/src/message_processor.rs:949
       app-server/src/in_process.rs:539
```

#### Evidence: Tokio worker stalls (dial9)

I recorded `codex exec` (a five-round, 4-parallel `exec_command` workload against a local mock Responses server) with [dial9](https://github.com/dial9-rs/dial9) attached to the `arg0` runtime (`--cfg tokio_unstable`, frame pointers, sched + CPU sampling). The two longest polls in the whole trace are both OS discovery. Runtime p99 poll time was about 0.75 ms.

```
LONG POLL  task=171  dur=73.39ms (97× runtime p99)   spawn: app-server/src/in_process.rs:496:36
  Command::output process.rs:1083
  retrieve lsb_release.rs:82
  get lsb_release.rs:10
  current_platform mod.rs:11
  ... LazyLock::force lazy_lock.rs:366
  current_runtime_metadata events.rs:1520
  track_initialize client.rs:413
  {async_fn#0} initialize_processor.rs:185
  {async_fn#0} message_processor.rs:949

LONG POLL  task=183  dur=61.9ms                       spawn: core-plugins/src/manager.rs:2936:13
  ... LazyLock::force lazy_lock.rs:366
  get_codex_user_agent default_client.rs:157
  default_headers default_client.rs:459
  http_request remote.rs:179
  {async_fn#0} remote_legacy.rs:137
```

The initialize-path poll was 85.1 ms in a second recording. Both long polls happen at the same time as the two concurrent `lsb_release` processes in the strace output above.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?


No model server is needed. The provider points at a closed port, and OS discovery happens before the first request.

```bash
cd codex-rs && cargo build --release --bin codex
mkdir -p /tmp/r/home /tmp/r/cwd && cd /tmp/r/cwd
CODEX_HOME=/tmp/r/home CODEX_API_KEY=dummy timeout 15 \
  strace -f -qq -tt -e trace=execve,exit_group -o /tmp/r/strace.txt \
  /path/to/codex-rs/target/release/codex exec --skip-git-repo-check \
  -c model_provider='"mock"' \
  -c 'model_providers.mock={name="mock",base_url="http://127.0.0.1:9/v1",wire_api="responses",requires_openai_auth=false,supports_websockets=false}' \
  hi
grep -E 'execve\("/usr/bin/(lsb_release|dpkg-query|getconf)"' /tmp/r/strace.txt | grep -E '= 0|unfinished' \
  | grep -oE '/usr/bin/[a-z_-]+' | sort | uniq -c
```

### What is the expected behavior?


The `os_info::Info` result is a per-process constant. One `codex` process should run OS discovery at most once. It should not do so from inside an async poll on a runtime worker, where it blocks other tasks scheduled on that worker.

The regression test added in #47038 ([`os_discovery_is_cached_without_freezing_user_agent_overrides`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/8094365e6a2da38be1cd37d58f308c496e3f7ac9/codex-rs/login/src/auth/default_client_tests.rs#L51-L108)) asserts `calls == ["getconf", "lsb_release"]`. It only calls `get_codex_user_agent()`, so it can't detect the analytics and otel caches running discovery again in the same process.

### Additional information

#### Environment

- built from source at `8094365e6a2da38be1cd37d58f308c496e3f7ac9` (includes #47038), `cargo build --release`; `main` at `e790ce2` still has the three statics
- `os_info` 3.14.0 (from `Cargo.lock`)
- Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, kernel 6.8.0-1061-aws, x86-64, 8 vCPU
- `codex exec`, default config, fresh `CODEX_HOME`


**Confirmed**
- Every stock `codex exec` run here executed `lsb_release`, `dpkg-query` and `getconf` three times each (3/3 runs).
- The three runs come from three separate `LazyLock<os_info::Info>` statics in `codex-otel`, `codex-login` and `codex-analytics`.
- The analytics and user-agent runs happen at the same time, on Tokio worker threads, inside async polls. One of them is in the `initialize` request path (`initialize_processor.rs:185` → `track_initialize`).

**Not measured / hypotheses**
- I haven't measured how much this delays the `initialize` response, or the first turn, compared with a single discovery. My expectation is that the cost is per process (tens of ms of wall time and three Python interpreter starts), not per request as in #36210.
- In long-lived `codex app-server` processes, this probably shows up as one startup cost, not an ongoing one. Workloads that start many short-lived `codex exec` processes pay it every time.
- I only tested Linux. On macOS and Windows, `os_info` uses different probes, so the cost may be different.

Related: #36210 (per-call discovery, now mostly addressed by #47038).

For comparison, a branch that routes all callers through one shared `LazyLock` (https://github.com/gpu004/codex/pull/2) runs each binary once per process (`lsb_release 1 / dpkg-query 1 / getconf 1`, 3/3 runs vs `3 / 3 / 3` on stock, same VM and command).

items.title: Windows desktop: simple greeting takes over 5 minutes; delays recur across chats after restart

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

items.body:
## Summary
The Windows desktop experience becomes progressively slow and sometimes stops responding. Starting a fresh chat, restarting the app and rebooting the PC did not prevent recurrence. This affects simple greetings and short questions, not just coding, file work or image generation.

## Environment
- Installed desktop version: 26.1007.71326
- Build: 20398; production channel
- Windows PC (exact Windows build not yet collected)
- Model shown in UI: GPT-6.1 Sol, Light
- Observed 15–16 October 2026, Australia/Perth (UTC+8)

## Steps / observed sequence
1. Work in an ongoing desktop conversation; responses become increasingly delayed and eventually fail.
2. Quit the app and reboot the PC.
3. Open another chat and continue work.
4. Return the next morning and send a simple hello, then Can we continue.
5. Wait over five minutes for a brief response, without any tool calls or file work in that turn.

## Verified timings
- Greeting/continuation turn on 16 October: 325,926 ms (5 min 25.926 sec); screenshot displayed Worked for 5m 24s.
- Three subsequent short replies: 48,335 ms, 49,924 ms and 49,322 ms, respectively, without tool calls.
- A later browser-tool attempt to open the Help Centre took approximately 552 seconds. This is a separate observation, not proof of the same cause.

## Earlier error
An earlier affected chat recorded: `Fatal error: application network permission was revoked`. It is unknown whether this explains the later latency; subsequent slow turns completed without a recorded error.

## Expected behavior
Simple greetings and short follow-up questions should receive responses promptly. Users should be able to resume ongoing work without repeatedly recreating context in new chats.

## Impact
Recurring delays make ongoing work impractical. Starting over has cost substantial time re-establishing context and correcting misunderstandings. Restarting and moving to another chat have not provided a lasting solution.

## Diagnostics / assistance requested
Please investigate whether server queueing, context processing, desktop transport or another issue explains these delays. These timings do not isolate the root cause. Exact private conversation/turn identifiers and screenshots are available through a private support channel; they are intentionally omitted from this public issue. No session-feedback upload reference has been generated yet.

The Help Centre automated support received the report but stated it could not create or confirm a ticket or transfer it to a human, and directed the user to this repository. Please advise how to supply the private request/session evidence securely and obtain a technical investigation.

items.title: Feature request: sparse local model catalogs that inherit native metadata and instructions

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: custom-model
labels.description: Issues related to custom model providers (including local models)

labels.name: config
labels.description: Issues involving config.toml, config keys, config merging, or config updates

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

CLI / app-server, with a custom provider and `model_catalog_json`.

### What feature would you like to see?

Allow entries in a **local** model catalog to specify a model `slug` and only the metadata fields they need to override. Omitted fields should inherit Codex's native model metadata and instructions, so users do not have to copy a complete model descriptor or maintain a fork of the bundled prompt.

For example:

```json
{
  "models": [
    {
      "slug": "example-model",
      "context_window": 1000000,
      "max_context_window": 1000000,
      "input_modalities": ["text", "image"]
    }
  ]
}
```

Custom provider and gateway integrations may know a model's context size, input modalities, and tool capabilities while wanting Codex to supply and update the remaining defaults. Requiring the full descriptor couples that small configuration change to unrelated catalog fields and prompt/schema updates.

This request concerns the entry format only. It does not change startup-only catalog loading, add a managed model allowlist, infer a gateway model's canonical identity, or change Responses Lite prompt semantics.

#### Current behavior and source-level reproduction

Inspected upstream commit: `e790ce271749ce431e446a9e2cc66485fe60f931`.

[`load_catalog_json`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/e790ce271749ce431e446a9e2cc66485fe60f931/codex-rs/core/src/config/mod.rs#L2197-L2220) deserializes the local file directly into `ModelsResponse`, requiring a full model descriptor.

A minimal reproduction recipe is to save the JSON above as `/tmp/codex-local-catalog.json`, then run:

```sh
codex -c 'model_catalog_json="/tmp/codex-local-catalog.json"' exec 'Reply OK'
```

The current loader is expected to reject this incomplete descriptor during configuration loading. This is a source-inspected reproduction recipe; I have **not** executed it with a binary built from the upstream commit above, and am not presenting a captured error log.

Desired behavior: accept the local overrides and supply omitted metadata through the existing native resolver. For unknown slugs, any generic fallback must be documented as a default, not a claim about the remote model's actual capabilities.

#### Possible compatibility contract

- Keep complete catalogs compatible with the existing wire parser, including its optional-field defaults.
- Fill only omitted top-level fields for sparse local entries; preserve explicit `false`, empty arrays, empty strings, and legal `null` values.
- Preserve native prompt precedence. In the reference prototype, explicit `model_messages`, or legacy `base_instructions` alone, replaces the entire message bundle. Omitting both inherits the native bundle. This avoids an inherited canonical template masking an explicit legacy prompt, but whole-bundle replacement is a design choice to discuss.
- Keep remote `ModelsResponse` parsing strict.
- Reuse bundled-model resolution and fallback logic rather than duplicating prompts or a model database.

### Additional information

**Reference patch:** https://gist.github.com/odinliu/e991948705c2d32364b7166c745fe529

The Gist includes the patch and a validation note. It is a prototype for discussion, not a PR or a request to merge unvalidated code. It includes parser tests and a focused catalog/resume test. `git apply --check` passed against the inspected upstream commit; compilation, tests, lint/formatting, and schema regeneration have **not** been run on that upstream base.

Open design questions include whether sparse entries need an explicit format discriminator, whether local unknown-key behavior should differ from the wire parser, and how fallback provenance should be reported for explicitly configured entries.

Related discussions:

- #28469 describes the full-descriptor/prompt maintenance burden, but primarily requests an enforceable model allowlist. This proposal does not implement enforcement.
- #21594 requests gateway-to-canonical model aliases. This proposal does not implement alias mapping.
- #38355 discusses Responses Lite prompt behavior and a catalog workaround. This proposal reduces catalog authoring overhead; it does not resolve that prompt-semantics issue.

I am opening this as a feature/design discussion in line with the current contribution guidelines, which direct external contributions to issues.

items.title: [Windows] Main process repeatedly crashes when closing built-in browser tabs: C0000005 / chrome.dll+0x532F638

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
## 问题与影响
Codex Windows 桌面端在代理关闭内置浏览器标签、清理 webview 时，整个主进程反复崩溃，持续中断工作。用户有时在其他应用中工作，关闭动作来自浏览器 API，不能归因于用户手动退出 Codex。升级应用后仍复发。

希望将此问题转交 Windows 桌面端／内置浏览器工程团队，用内部符号核对原生窗口销毁与相关数据宿主的生命周期，并提供修复版本或最小补充诊断要求。用户希望继续使用内置浏览器；更换外部浏览器不应被视为已修复。

## 环境
- Windows 11 x64，系统版本 26200。
- 应用版本：26.1007.71326。
- MSIX 包身份：OpenAI.Codex；包版本：26.1007.9446.0；主进程：ChatGPT.exe。
- 内置 chrome.dll 文件版本：155.0.8059.40。
- 此前应用 26.1007.21434／包 26.1007.2314.0 也发生过类似闪退。

## 实际场景与复现边界
1. 代理在真实任务中正常使用 Codex 内置浏览器。
2. 浏览器 API 通过 Target.closeTarget 关闭标签，日志记录 reason=target-close。
3. webview disposed、guest torn down、closed browser sidebar page 后，主进程发生原生异常并整体退出。

已记录事件：2026-10-14 19:03；10-15 09:49、09:55、12:06；10-16 09:56、11:19、11:35（均 UTC+8）。不是每次关闭都复现。空白页连续打开／关闭测试没有触发问题，不能作为真实任务已修复的依据。

预期：关闭内置浏览器标签应正常释放相关对象，主应用及其他任务保持运行。

## 最新一次完整捕获：2026-10-16 11:35（UTC+8）
使用独立于 Codex 进程树运行的微软 ProcDump 捕获，转储只在本机用微软调试引擎离线分析：
- 11:35:01 首次机会异常，Mini 转储完整写入：45,327,652 字节，耗时 1.1 秒。
- 11:35:03 进程以 0xC0000005 退出，退出转储完整写入：42,412,466 字节，耗时 0.4 秒。
- 以上两份转储属于同一次崩溃，并非两次事件。
- Crashpad sidecar 同时记录 capture_kind=crash、osarch=x86_64、ptype=browser。

原生异常签名：
~~~text
Thread:          CrBrowserMain
Exception/exit:  0xC0000005 (read access violation)
Module:          bundled chrome.dll
Fault RVA:       0x532F638
Instruction:     cmp qword ptr [rax+0x20], rdx
RAX:             0xEFEFEFEFEFEFEFEF
Computed read:   0xEFEFEFEFEFEFF00F (noncanonical)
Exception record reports attempted read address as 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF.
Direct caller:   chrome.dll+0xAAE589C -> chrome.dll+0x532F600
~~~

10月16日11:19那次未写完的转储中，已恢复并交叉核对异常／线程上下文和模块记录；其故障 RVA 与 EF 指针值和本次完整转储一致。

## 堆栈与查询对象证据
下载精确匹配的 Windows 公共 PDB 后，堆栈显示原生窗口销毁路径：
~~~text
win32u!NtUserDestroyWindow
  -> user32!_fnNCDESTROY
  -> user32!DispatchClientMessage
  -> Chromium 窗口／视图清理回调
  -> chrome.dll+0x532F638 非法读取
~~~

故障处 RDX 指向的键可读取为 BrowserActions::kDataKeyImpl；邻近字符串为 Chromium 源路径 chrome/browser/ui/browser_actions.cc。直接调用点的反汇编显示：从接收对象偏移 0x7A8 取指针，偏移 0xA8 取得关联数据宿主，随后查询树结构时解引用 EF 指针。

## 判断与限制
高度怀疑窗口／视图销毁期间的对象生命周期错误或释放后使用（use-after-free），尚未证实具体被释放对象及其分配／释放堆栈。

匹配此 chrome.dll 的私有 PDB 在所查的微软／Electron 公共符号服务中不可用。因此，调试器以邻近导出名加巨大偏移显示的 V8／Node 函数名不应被当作准确责任函数。请使用内部精确符号确认，而不要仅依据邻近导出名定责。

chrome.dll SHA-256：
~~~text
CE6D04CC948E034C5F18D116A76DBB2CDF84B068C85101E53D168FBB33DADD60
~~~

没有修改安装目录代码、GPU 设置、输入法、账号数据库或业务项目。当前没有经过验证的本机修复。

相关既有报告包括 #30178、#46644，但它们描述的触发阶段／故障偏移不同，暂不能认定为同一根因；本报告补充当前版本的关闭窗口签名和已捕获的销毁调用链。

## 隐私与后续材料
本次仅公开脱敏后的技术摘要。原始转储、完整日志、聊天内容、业务网址、账号信息和本机路径均未上传。原始转储含潜在敏感内存，用户明确要求暂时仅保留在本机。如工程团队确实需要，请先说明最小数据要求和官方安全提交渠道，再由用户决定。

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1007.9446.0

### What subscription do you have?

Pro

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 Pro, 64-bit

### What issue are you seeing?

The entire Codex window repeatedly disappears during portfolio publishing and when I enter /feedback. Restarting did not help. Publishing also reports: write_stdin rejected: approval required by policy, but AskForApproval::Granular.sandbox_approval is false, although “Ask for approval” is selected. Version 26.1007.9446.0 is listed under ChatGPT in Windows Installed apps.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Open the portfolio publishing chat with “Ask for approval” selected.
2. Ask Codex to publish the portfolio.
3. Publishing reports: write_stdin rejected: approval required by policy, but AskForApproval::Granular.sandbox_approval is false.
4. The entire app window closes during publishing.
5. Reopen the app and try /feedback. The entire window closes again.

The closures have happened repeatedly. Restarting has not resolved them.

### What is the expected behavior?

The app should remain open during publishing and feedback submission. When an action requires approval, it should show an approval prompt or explain the restriction without closing.

### Additional information

_No response_

items.title: [Workaround] Codex Desktop reconnection loop — Starting Ollama restored connectivity

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: custom-model
labels.description: Issues related to custom model providers (including local models)

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

items.body:
## Summary

Codex Desktop on macOS became unusable on October 15, 2026, at approximately 11:30 AM JST.

The application repeatedly displayed:

- Reconnecting... waiting for network
- Connection failed: error sending request
- Error running remote compact task: Connection failed: error sending request

Codex continuously attempted to reconnect but failed, making it impossible to continue working.

The problem persisted for more than 24 hours.

Changing networks, disabling VPN/proxy settings, and restarting Codex did not resolve the issue.

ChatGPT and Claude continued to work normally on the same Mac.

## Investigation

I examined the Codex Desktop logs and found repeated WebSocket connection failures.

The logs contained errors such as:

```
Codex app-server websocket closed (code=1006)
```

```
startup websocket prewarm setup failed:
stream disconnected before completion:
Connection refused (os error 61)
```

I also discovered that my Codex configuration contained:

```toml
openai_base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/codex/v1"
```

However, nothing was listening on port 11434.

Running:

```bash
lsof -nP -iTCP:11434 -sTCP:LISTEN
```

Returned no results.

Running:

```bash
curl -v --connect-timeout 3 http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/version
```

Resulted in:

```
Connection refused
curl: (7) Failed to connect to 127.0.0.1 port 11434
```

## Solution That Worked

I started Ollama on macOS:

```bash
open -a Ollama
```

Then verified connectivity:

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/version
```

The request successfully returned:

```json
{"version":"0.40.4"}
```

HTTP status: 200 OK.

**After starting Ollama and restoring connectivity to port 11434, Codex Desktop resumed normal operation.**

No changes to the Codex configuration were required.

## Suggested Workaround

For users experiencing repeated Codex connection failures who have configured Codex to use a local Ollama endpoint:

1. Check whether Ollama is running.
2. Start or restart Ollama if necessary.
3. Verify that port 11434 is accessible.
4. Retry Codex.

This procedure successfully restored Codex functionality in my environment.

I cannot confirm that all Codex reconnection failures are related to Ollama. However, users with similar local API configurations may benefit from checking whether their Ollama service is running.

## Suggested Improvement for Codex

Codex should provide more specific error messages when a configured local API endpoint is unavailable.

In this case, the application repeatedly displayed:

```
Reconnecting... waiting for network
```

And:

```
Connection failed: error sending request
```

These messages suggested a general network connectivity issue, even though the logs identified a connection refusal involving a configured local endpoint.

Instead of repeatedly attempting to reconnect without explaining the problem, Codex should detect when a configured local API endpoint is unavailable and display a message such as:

```
Unable to connect to the configured API endpoint:
http://127.0.0.1:11434

Connection refused.

Please verify that the local API server is running.
```

This would allow users to identify and resolve the problem much faster.

## Environment

- Platform: macOS
- Application: Codex Desktop
- Codex Desktop build number found in logs: 20398
- Local Codex app-server version found in logs: 0.162.0-alpha.17.2
- Ollama version: 0.40.4
- Configured local API endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/codex/v1
- Issue started: October 15, 2026, approximately 11:30 AM JST

## Conclusion

**Starting Ollama restored Codex Desktop functionality after more than 24 hours of repeated connection failures.**

The precise reason the problem initially appeared on October 15 has not been established.

However, the connection refusal to the configured local endpoint was confirmed, and Codex resumed working after Ollama was started.

I hope this information helps other users experiencing similar issues and assists the Codex development team in improving error reporting and connection diagnostics.

The main improvement requested is that Codex should distinguish between external network failures and unavailable locally configured API endpoints, rather than displaying the same generic reconnection error for both situations.

items.title: [Bug] Chrome/Edge extension v1.26 forces web-sidepanel, breaks local browser-control mode; Edge store extension ID missing from CSP frame-ancestors

labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
﻿## Summary

Two regressions in the latest Chrome/Edge browser extension (v1.26.x, auto-updated 2026-10-16):

1. **Local browser-control mode removed** — The side panel now force-loads `chatgpt.com` inside an iframe (`codex-work-sidepanel.html`). The previous local mode, where the panel drove the browser directly via the native host, is gone. There is no user-facing toggle to switch back.

2. **Edge store extension blocked by CSP** — The Edge-addons build (extension ID `odlomjlbamekndcpllcnffbgeohgkmjh`) is not included in the `frame-ancestors` CSP directive returned by `chatgpt.com`, so the side panel fails with "ChatGPT couldn't load" / "chatgpt.com refused to connect". The Chrome Web Store build (`hehggadaopoacecdllhhajmbjkdcmajg`) works because its ID is whitelisted.

## Reproduction

### Issue 1: Local mode gone
1. Install extension v1.26.x on Chrome or Edge
2. Click the toolbar icon to open the side panel
3. Panel loads `chatgpt.com` web UI instead of the local browser-control interface
4. `chrome.storage.session` key `codexSidePanelDestination` is set to `work_sidepanel`; controlled by remote Statsig gate `codex_chrome_sidepanel_work_mode` with no local override

### Issue 2: Edge CSP block
1. Install the Edge-addons build of ChatGPT extension (ID `odlomjlbamekndcpllcnffbgeohgkmjh`)
2. Open the side panel
3. Console error:
   ```
   Framing 'https://chatgpt.com/' violates the following Content Security Policy directive:
   "frame-ancestors 'self' chrome-extension://hehggadaopoacecdllhhajmbjkdcmajg
   chrome-extension://iaiigpefkbhgjcmcmffmfkpmhemdhdnj
   chrome-extension://lfkehkpjohcoelkpembgemeipeppanef".
   The request has been blocked.
   ```
4. Native messaging tunnel shows `state: connected` (`com.openai.codexextension`), so the extension itself is bound and working — only the iframe embedding is rejected.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11
- Codex Desktop App: `OpenAI.Codex_26.1013.3656.0_x64` (display name "ChatGPT")
- Chrome extension: `hehggadaopoacecdllhhajmbjkdcmajg` v1.26.1005.11759
- Edge extension: `odlomjlbamekndcpllcnffbgeohgkmjh` v1.26.1006.11559
- Native host manifest: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\extension\com.openai.codexextension.json` (already lists both extension IDs in `allowed_origins`)
- The Edge registry key `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Edge\NativeMessagingHosts\com.openai.codexextension` was missing on a fresh install; had to be created manually (mirroring the Chrome key). This may be a separate installer bug.

## Expected Behavior

1. Provide a user setting (or respect the existing native-host presence) to use the local browser-control side panel instead of the forced web iframe.
2. Add `chrome-extension://odlomjlbamekndcpllcnffbgeohgkmjh/` to the `frame-ancestors` CSP allowlist on `chatgpt.com` so the official Edge build works.
3. Ensure the Edge installer registers the `com.openai.codexextension` native messaging host in `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Edge\NativeMessagingHosts`, not only under Chrome.

## Workaround

Install the Chrome Web Store build (`hehggadaopoacecdllhhajmbjkdcmajg`) into Edge via the Chrome Web Store; its ID is already in the CSP allowlist so the side panel loads.

items.title: Document a supported third-party attachment and graceful-pause path for tasks already owned by Codex Desktop

labels.name: documentation
labels.description: Improvements or additions to documentation

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
## Integration / documentation question

We are preparing a small user-authorized macOS App Sandbox utility that monitors Codex quota and is intended for Mac App Store distribution. We need to coordinate tasks already running in Codex Desktop without killing processes, copying credentials, editing task databases, or starting a second task owner.

We have read the [App Server goal APIs](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server) and inspected the public source reference `6b991972c5b539198dcea9bac4fc14e57559c3af`. The goal status type includes `paused`. The request processor appears to send its response and goal update before applying runtime effects, and the paused runtime branch clears active goal accounting. We have not run these mutations against live user tasks or established that this public-source revision matches the installed Desktop runtime.

## Questions

1. Is there a supported transport and authorization flow for a separately signed sandboxed third-party macOS client to attach to the same app-server/runtime that owns an existing Desktop task? Please point to the supported API or confirm that this integration is currently not supported. We do not assume the first-party remote-control pairing flow is a public third-party API.
2. On that same runtime, what does `thread/goal/set(status=paused)` guarantee about the current turn, active tool operations, descendant agents and future goal continuation? What supported event/readback demonstrates that work is quiescent? Is there a graceful-pause mechanism for ordinary tasks without a goal?
3. What is the supported way to recognize an explicit user continuation of that task, so a quota guard can avoid immediately repeating the same pause, while retaining protection for other tasks? Please also identify any distribution/authentication restrictions applicable to this integration.

## Scope and privacy

This is an integration/documentation question, not a claim that the goal API is defective or a request to bypass sandbox, ownership, or service limits. We can adapt to an equivalent supported protocol; we are not requiring a bespoke nonce or safe-point schema. No private account IDs, task content, local paths, credentials or raw logs are included.

Related ownership context: #52675 reports contention between multiple app-server instances. That is another user's report, not our reproduction or an official statement of support. Our question is specifically about a supported attachment to the existing owner, not taking over its writer lock.

Submitted with AI assistance and the account owner's authorization.

items.title: Notion plugin examples retain factual and connector-call errors

labels.name: documentation
labels.description: Improvements or additions to documentation

labels.name: skills
labels.description: Issues related to skills

items.body:
### What is the type of issue?

Documentation is incorrect; Example code is not working.

### What is the issue?

Several public Notion plugin examples on `openai/plugins` current `main` still contain factual errors, obsolete call shapes, or write steps that exceed the example user's request. PR [openai/plugins#256](https://github.com/openai/plugins/pull/256) fixed some live-app contracts, but the following remain. The plugin repository has Issues disabled and external PR creation restricted, so I am reporting them here for routing.

1. [Executive review](https://github.com/openai/plugins/blob/main/plugins/notion/skills/notion-meeting-intelligence/examples/executive-review.md): “94% uptime (above 95% SLA)” should say below. The agenda labeled 90 minutes adds up to 100 (15+20+20+15+15+15).
2. [Customer meeting](https://github.com/openai/plugins/blob/main/plugins/notion/skills/notion-meeting-intelligence/examples/customer-meeting.md): October 17, 2025 was Friday, not Thursday.
3. [Spec parsing](https://github.com/openai/plugins/blob/main/plugins/notion/skills/notion-spec-to-implementation/reference/spec-parsing.md): a 100 MB upload limit does not imply progress and cancellation controls. A parse/plan-only request should not create clarification tasks or comments unless those writes are authorized.
4. [Progress tracking](https://github.com/openai/plugins/blob/main/plugins/notion/skills/notion-spec-to-implementation/reference/progress-tracking.md): `Related Tasks CONTAINS` is presented as executable SQL without checking the actual data-source schema and relation encoding. `12/28` rounds to 43%, not 44%.
5. [API feature example](https://github.com/openai/plugins/blob/main/plugins/notion/skills/notion-spec-to-implementation/examples/api-feature.md): the user asks only for an implementation plan, but the example creates task pages, writes back to the spec, and reports 20 tasks created. Those writes should be separate authorized steps and reported only after tool confirmation. `insert_content_after` should use the current `update-page` contract or be marked conceptual.
6. [Project decision example](https://github.com/openai/plugins/blob/main/plugins/notion/skills/notion-meeting-intelligence/examples/project-decision.md): the comment call uses `parent` rather than `page_id`. Plain-text `@Sarah` etc. are not confirmed user mentions or notifications.
7. [Task creation](https://github.com/openai/plugins/blob/main/plugins/notion/skills/notion-spec-to-implementation/reference/task-creation.md): the `notion-create-pages` example omits the required `pages` array. Relation/person/date values should be shaped from a fetched live data-source schema.

Suggested checks: arithmetic/date assertions; plan-only synthetic runs make no Notion writes; explicitly requested writes use the current connector schema and actual data-source fields; summaries distinguish proposed steps from confirmed writes. This report uses only public examples and includes no user workspace content.

### Where did you find it?

The seven `openai/plugins` file links above, under `plugins/notion/skills/` on current `main` (checked 2026-10-16).

### What issue are you seeing?

The ChatGPT Work/Codex browser agent and browser extension stopped connecting after previously working correctly.

The browser agent had been successfully controlling open WordPress tabs in Google Chrome. On October 15, 2026, the connection suddenly stopped working.

The following errors and messages have appeared:

- “This is open in another app. Close it there to continue here.”
- “Unable to find the connected browser.”
- “RPC INTERNAL”
- “chatgpt.com refused to connect.”
- “ChatGPT for Chrome is coming soon. The ChatGPT extension is rolling out gradually. In the meantime, you can use ChatGPT on the web.”

The extension is shown as installed under Settings > Computer Use > Google Chrome. It has permission to access the WordPress and hosting websites being used.

The same account and ChatGPT Team workspace are being used. ChatGPT works normally in a regular browser tab. My usage limits and workspace credits are available.

The issue began shortly after I purchased additional workspace credits or refreshed the account session. I cannot confirm that the purchase caused the problem, but the timing coincided with the browser access disappearing.

Troubleshooting already completed:

1. Closed and reopened Chrome.
2. Restarted the browser and Windows computer.
3. Closed other ChatGPT conversations and applications that might have been using the browser.
4. Removed and reinstalled the ChatGPT browser extension.
5. Signed out and signed back in using the same ChatGPT account and Team workspace.
6. Tested the extension in Microsoft Edge.
7. Confirmed that ChatGPT works normally in a standard browser tab.
8. Confirmed that usage limits and workspace credits remain available.
9. Tested again after waiting several hours.

The issue occurs in both Chrome and Edge, so it does not appear to be specific to one browser.

Expected behavior:
The browser agent should connect to the installed extension and regain control of the authorized browser tabs, as it did previously.

Actual behavior:
The agent cannot locate or connect to the browser. It returns RPC INTERNAL or displays a message saying the Chrome extension is “coming soon,” even though this feature had already been enabled and working on my account.

Please investigate whether the Browser/Computer Use entitlement or connection associated with my ChatGPT Team workspace was reset or lost after the account session or credit update.

Feedback ID:
no-active-thread-01a142b0-1994-7091-9732-3bf806c7a9e6

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Start Google Chrome on Windows and sign in to chatgpt.com using the affected ChatGPT Team account and workspace.
2. Confirm that the ChatGPT browser extension is installed and has permission to access the current website.
3. Open an authenticated WordPress administration tab.
4. Open ChatGPT Work/Codex and start a new conversation.
5. Ask the agent to inspect or interact with the open WordPress tab.
6. The agent attempts to connect to the browser but fails with “Unable to find the connected browser” or “RPC INTERNAL.”
7. Opening the browser extension may also display “chatgpt.com refused to connect” or “ChatGPT for Chrome is coming soon. The ChatGPT extension is rolling out gradually.”
8. Repeat the test after restarting Chrome and signing back in. The same failure occurs.
9. Install and test the extension in Microsoft Edge using the same account. The same connection failure occurs there as well.

The issue is reproducible every time the agent attempts to connect to the browser. The same workflow worked correctly before October 15, 2026.

### What is the expected behavior?

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_

items.title: Desktop keeps its own session-to-project map in .codex-global-state.json and ignores (later reverts) thread/metadata/update project changes

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From "About Codex" dialog)?

ChatGPT/Codex desktop app `26.1007.9446.0` (Microsoft Store package `OpenAI.Codex_26.1007.9446.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0`). Bundled CLI: `codex-cli 0.162.1`.

### What subscription do you have?

Not included in this report.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 Pro, x64.

### What issue are you seeing?

Session→project membership has two sources of truth, and the desktop's copy wins — so any project change made through the documented app-server API is invisible on the desktop, and can later be silently reverted by the desktop.

Concretely, after calling `thread/metadata/update {threadId, projectId}` (the same RPC the desktop itself sends when moving a thread):

1. `state_5.sqlite` `threads.project_id` is updated (this column is documented as canonical — `codex-rs/rollout/src/list.rs` calls it "Canonical project assignment in SQLite-owned metadata"), and `thread/list` filtered by `projectId` returns the thread under the new project. Any non-desktop client sees the move.
2. The desktop sidebar keeps showing the thread under the old project, because the desktop reads its own persisted state in `$CODEX_HOME/.codex-global-state.json` instead of the app-server record:
   - `thread-project-assignments`: threadId → `{projectKind, projectId}` keyed by the desktop's own legacy project UUIDs
   - `sidebar-project-thread-orders`: per-project thread ordering used to render the sidebar
   - `local-projects`: the desktop's own project entities, mapped to app-server project ids only via `app-server-project-id-by-legacy-project-id-by-host`
3. Worse: with `app-server-projects-migration-by-host.<host>.threadAssignmentsMigrated = false`, the desktop queues thread ids in `pendingThreadAssignmentIds` and pushes its (stale) local assignment back to the app-server during migration. A thread moved externally was reverted to its old project this way — the API change just disappears.

So a third-party client implementing the documented protocol cannot move a thread in a way the desktop honors. The only workarounds are writing the desktop's private state file out-of-band (lost within seconds while the app is running, since it rewrites the file from memory), or moving from the desktop UI.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On Windows with the desktop app installed, pick a thread that belongs to project A (visible in the desktop sidebar).
2. Call `thread/metadata/update` with `{threadId, projectId: <project B>}` against an app-server instance on the same `$CODEX_HOME`.
3. `thread/list` with `projectId: B` now includes the thread; the desktop sidebar still shows it under A (verified after a full restart of the app).
4. Let the desktop app keep running; its `pendingThreadAssignmentIds` migration eventually pushes A back, and `threads.project_id` in `state_5.sqlite` is reverted.

Also reproducible in the opposite direction: the desktop's own move (its local state + its own `thread/metadata/update` call) is invisible to other clients until its migration queue catches up, since the two stores only sync one way, on the desktop's schedule.

### Expected behavior

One canonical store for thread→project membership. The app-server state (`threads.project_id` + the existing `thread/project/updated` notification) is already there and already published — the desktop should treat it as the source of truth (or at least subscribe to `thread/project/updated` and reconcile its local mirror), instead of maintaining a parallel assignment map that external changes cannot reach and that overwrites them.

Related reports that look like symptoms of the same split: #48728 (app-server-created tasks missing from their projects), #51477 (chats disappear from groups while saved assignments remain), #46987 / #47007 (global-state corruption loses project grouping while sessions survive — because grouping lives in this file rather than the DB), #48641.

items.body:
## Problem

On Windows, supported browser control remains unreliable after an actual uninstall/reinstall of the managed Browser plugin. Chrome discovery succeeds, but listing tabs fails before any website access. The in-app browser can still read a local WebGL project page, while external-page reads and interactions time out. This is blocking a previously working browser workflow.

## Verified environment

- Incident date: 2026-10-16, UTC+8.
- Windows desktop package: `OpenAI.Codex 26.1007.9446.0`.
- Managed Browser plugin: `browser@openai-bundled`, version `26.1007.71326`.
- Chrome extension and in-app browser backends are discoverable.
- Browser operations below used the entry point prescribed by the installed Browser skill: its official `browser-client.mjs` through the bundled Node tool.
- Subscription tier and exact Windows/Chrome build are not included because they were not verified for this report.

## Reproduction and actual results

### Chrome: failure before navigating to a website

1. Initialize the supported browser runtime and select `agent.browsers.get('chrome')`.
2. Browser selection and `chrome.nameSession(...)` succeed; browser discovery lists Chrome.
3. Call `chrome.user.openTabs()`: after approximately 21.4 seconds, it returns `nodeRepl.fetch request failed`.
4. Following the documented troubleshooting procedure, wait at least two seconds and retry once: same result.
5. `chrome.tabs.list()` also returns `nodeRepl.fetch request failed` after approximately 21.4 seconds.

No website navigation is reached in these Chrome reproductions. Discovery success is therefore not evidence that live browser control is healthy.

### In-app browser: local control versus external pages

- `iab.tabs.list()` succeeds. Reading the existing local project page's AX succeeds; the latest comparison took approximately 0.7 seconds. Earlier controlled checks on the local WebGL page also succeeded for DOM reads, screenshot capture, and opening/closing its help panel.
- A fresh official Hunyuan creation page initially exposes its UI, including version V3.1. One click on the visible multi-image label followed by an AX read hits the 30-second tool timeout and resets the tool kernel. Whether the click completed is unknown.
- A separate control site, `https://example.com/`, also fails: creating a tab, navigating, and reading AX in one call hits a 30-second tool timeout. After recovery, the tab inventory shows the expected URL and title `Example Domain`, so navigation reached page metadata, but successful content access is not established.
- Reading that same Example Domain tab through the documented DOM snapshot API, without reloading, then hits a 20-second tool timeout and resets the kernel. No click was attempted on this control site because no usable page state was returned.

These are observed client/tool timeout limits; they do not establish which internal request is stalled. One external control site is not proof that every external website fails.

## Recovery and diagnostics already performed

- The four official read-only checks for Chrome running, installed browsers, extension installation, and native-host manifest all exit successfully. Prior detailed checks also reported extension installed/enabled and matching native-host registration.
- The official helper opened the extension's profile window successfully, but follow-up website control still failed.
- A previously authorized Chrome restart completed, but did not restore stable control.
- The exact managed Browser plugin was actually removed and immediately re-added using the bundled official Codex CLI. Both commands exited successfully. Post-install listing confirms installed/enabled and the same version; the cache has 384 files and its public manifest matches the verified bundled source. Related Chrome/Computer Use plugins were retained.
- Post-reinstall control checks still fail as described above. It is not established that all already-running control components hot-loaded the reinstalled package.
- Filtered application diagnostics also contain IAB missing-route/frame errors and a focus-emulation timeout. Their causal relationship to the Chrome fetch failures is unknown. Separate durable-connection timeouts are present, but that connection's role in browser control has not been established.

## Expected behavior / requested investigation

Tab listing and page-state requests should complete reliably, or report an actionable, sanitized failure identifying the stalled connection layer. Please investigate the Chrome fetch failure before navigation and the IAB external-page timeouts, and provide a supported repair/update or supported request-correlation diagnostics.

Potentially related: #54229 reports the same desktop package and approximately 21-second browser tab-list fetch failures; #51659 reports another browser request-path timeout. This report does not establish that their proposed causes apply here.

No private project content, images, account identifiers, credentials, cookies, personal paths, raw logs, full session IDs, or session transcripts are attached. No safety or permission bypass was attempted.

items.body:
## Integration / documentation question

We are preparing a small user-authorized macOS App Sandbox utility that monitors Codex quota and is intended for Mac App Store distribution. We need to coordinate tasks already running in Codex Desktop without killing processes, copying credentials, editing task databases, or starting a second task owner.

We have read the [App Server goal APIs](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server) and inspected the public source reference `6b991972c5b539198dcea9bac4fc14e57559c3af`. The goal status type includes `paused`. The request processor appears to send its response and goal update before applying runtime effects, and the paused runtime branch clears active goal accounting. We have not run these mutations against live user tasks or established that this public-source revision matches the installed Desktop runtime.

## Questions

1. Is there a supported transport and authorization flow for a separately signed sandboxed third-party macOS client to attach to the same app-server/runtime that owns an existing Desktop task? Please point to the supported API or confirm that this integration is currently not supported. We do not assume the first-party remote-control pairing flow is a public third-party API.
2. On that same runtime, what does `thread/goal/set(status=paused)` guarantee about the current turn, active tool operations, descendant agents and future goal continuation? What supported event/readback demonstrates that work is quiescent? Is there a graceful-pause mechanism for ordinary tasks without a goal?
3. What is the supported way to recognize an explicit user continuation of that task, so a quota guard can avoid immediately repeating the same pause, while retaining protection for other tasks? Please also identify any distribution/authentication restrictions applicable to this integration.

## Scope and privacy

This is an integration/documentation question, not a claim that the goal API is defective or a request to bypass sandbox, ownership, or service limits. We can adapt to an equivalent supported protocol; we are not requiring a bespoke nonce or safe-point schema. No private account IDs, task content, local paths, credentials or raw logs are included.

Related ownership context: #52675 reports contention between multiple app-server instances. That is another user's report, not our reproduction or an official statement of support. Our question is specifically about a supported attachment to the existing owner, not taking over its writer lock.

Submitted with AI assistance and the account owner's authorization.

items.title: Long ChatGPT Conversations Cannot Be Reopened or Read on Android

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

items.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

Some long-running ordinary ChatGPT conversations cannot be reopened in the Android app, especially conversations with extensive histories or those that have reached or approached their model context limit

This is not just an inability to send a new message or continue generating a response — in affected conversations, I cannot even open the saved conversation to read earlier messages

Other conversations still open normally, so the failure appears selective rather than a general inability to access ChatGPT

These histories contain accumulated research notes and important work, making loss of read access a significant reliability problem

Context-window exhaustion and access to previously saved chat history are different concerns — reaching a model's context limit should not make that history unreadable

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Open the official ChatGPT app on Android
2. From conversation history, select an existing ordinary ChatGPT conversation with an unusually long history, especially one that has reached or approached its context limit
3. Attempt to reopen the conversation to review earlier messages, without needing to send another prompt
4. Observe that the affected conversation does not load into a usable view and the saved messages cannot be read
5. Open another, shorter conversation in the same app session and compare the result

The exact message-count or payload-size threshold, as well as whether every affected conversation behaves the same way on Web, have not been established

### What is the expected behavior?

Previously saved conversations should remain accessible in a read-only capacity even when the model cannot accept further context or continue the thread

The Android app should display recent saved messages promptly, load older history progressively where needed, and provide a meaningful, recoverable error if loading fails

Reaching a context limit should not prevent a user from opening, reading, or copying earlier content

### Additional information

- Product: ordinary ChatGPT conversations on Android, not Codex Remote
- Symptom: failure to reopen and read selected large or context-full histories, not simply a generation limit
- Exact Android app version, failed request IDs, affected conversation links, and cross-client comparison: not yet confirmed for this report
- Root cause is unknown — possibilities worth investigating include history retrieval, pagination, response-size or timeout handling, mobile state reconstruction, and rendering or memory pressure
- Please distinguish model continuation limits, history-loading failures, and actual connectivity errors in product diagnostics

Related public report involving ordinary ChatGPT Android long-history retrieval:
https://community.openai.com/t/long-conversations-fail-to-load-after-fresh-installation-network-connection-lost-timeout/1405867

A separate, related ChatGPT Android thread-loading report is also present on GitHub:
https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/51765

This issue is intentionally limited to Android long-conversation history accessibility and does not address other model-selection or desktop errors

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1013.3656.0 (issue first appeared on 26.1007.9446.0)

### What subscription do you have?

None - API-key auth with a third-party OpenAI-compatible provider via local proxy. No ChatGPT account. This setup worked daily until 2026-10-14.

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64 (Windows 11 Pro), WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04

### What issue are you seeing?

Since the core-engine auto-update on 2026-10-14 ~16:44 local (binaries under %LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex\bin), launching the desktop app with the agent environment set to "Windows Subsystem for Linux" shows a blocking modal and the app never starts:

Unable to load organization settings
(The app is paused until organization settings can be safely loaded. Network, proxy, or firewall may be blocking access.)
[Retry] [Sign out] [Quit]

- Retry loops back to the same modal.
- "Sign out" completes (auth.json gets rewritten to just the API key) but the modal returns.
- With agent environment = Windows, the app starts normally on the same machine.
- Reproduced on app 26.1007.9446.0 and still on 26.1013.3656.0 (tested 2026-10-16).

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Windows 11 Pro (26200, x64) + WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04. Codex App from Microsoft Store (package OpenAI.Codex).
2. Use a custom model provider with API-key auth: config.toml has model_provider = "custom", base_url = http://127.0.0.1:<local-proxy>/v1, requires_openai_auth = true; auth.json contains only OPENAI_API_KEY. No ChatGPT account login. This is how the app has been used for months, including on 2026-10-13 and 2026-10-14 with agent environment = WSL.
3. Set agent environment to "Windows Subsystem for Linux" and restart the app.
4. The "Unable to load organization settings" modal blocks the app (Retry/Sign out loop).

### What is the expected behavior?

The app should start with the WSL agent environment under API-key / custom-provider auth, as it did on 2026-10-13/14 before the 2026-10-14 core-engine update.

### Additional information

Diagnostics already done (to save triage time):

1. Likely red herrings - the following appear at high volume on WORKING days (2026-10-13/14) as well:
   - GET /wham/usage and /settings/user -> HTTP 432 "Workspace routing is unavailable" (hundreds/day)
   - "Sign in to ChatGPT to start a durable thread" (tens of thousands/day)
   - bundled_plugins_marketplace_add_failed "marketplace `openai-primary-runtime` is reserved and cannot be added from this source" (thousands/day)
2. During a gated WSL launch, the local app-server does come up: hostId=local reaches connected, host-app-server-projects migration completes, thread/read is served. So the WSL core itself starts; the gating happens on the app/render side.
3. Tried without success: removing stale [marketplaces.*] sections from config.toml; preferred_auth_method = "apikey" in config.toml.
4. Resetting the embedded browser profile (LocalCache/Roaming/Codex/web/Codex/codex-browser-app renamed) stopped the modal in Windows agent environment, but WSL agent environment still gates afterwards.
5. New in 26.1013 logs: "read remote plugin details: chatgpt authentication required for remote plugin catalog; api key auth is not supported" (method=plugin/read), 28 occurrences. It also appears in Windows mode without blocking there.
6. Side bug: during some gated launches the desktop file logger creates no new session log files at all under LocalCache/Local/Codex/Logs/<date>/, which makes diagnosis much harder.
7. Config drift: after gated launches, runCodexInWindowsSubsystemForLinux in config.toml was observed flipped back to false on its own.

Questions:
- With the account-required direction (plugin catalog), is desktop usage with a custom provider / API key still supported?
- If the WSL agent environment now requires ChatGPT auth, please surface that explicitly instead of the generic "organization settings" modal.

### What version of the Codex App are you using?

Desktop product **26.1013.31256**; Windows package **OpenAI.Codex 26.1013.3656.0**; active bundled core **0.163.0-alpha.10.2**. Versions were read from installed metadata and the active bundled executable after a full app quit/reopen.

### What subscription do you have?

Not included in this public report; can provide privately if needed.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows x64. PowerShell OSVersion: `Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26300.0`.

### What issue are you seeing?

A fresh task created by **Your dot** on its connected Windows computer fails before it can read a browser page title:

```text
node_repl kernel exited unexpectedly
Error: failed to prepare MXC sandbox: MXC requires nonempty Unicode host SystemDrive
```

The task started with **workspace-write and automatic approval review**. Its first browser call failed. It made no permission changes and tried no alternate route.

This persists after updating and fully restarting the desktop app. A direct local chat on the same computer, tested after that restart with restricted workspace-write permissions, successfully initialized the browser controller, opened example.com, and read **Example Domain**.

The Windows host has a nonempty SystemDrive value. The new diagnostic explicitly reports that the value is unavailable at MXC preparation on the DOT route.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Have Your dot create a fresh task on its connected Windows computer.
2. Leave the task's default workspace-write permissions and automatic approval review in place.
3. Ask the supported local browser tool to open https://example.com/ and report its title.
4. Observe the SystemDrive error above and Node kernel exit before a title is returned.

This was a newly created DOT task after the update, not continuation of an old failed chat.

### What is the expected behavior?

DOT-created tasks should initialize the Windows browser controller and read the page title under their assigned permissions, as the direct local chat does.

### Additional information

- Manually switching affected chats to **Full Access** has been a working workaround in this installation. DOT-created tasks start with Custom/workspace-write despite a saved Full Access preference.
- The earlier installed core, **0.162.0-alpha.17.2**, reported the less specific `MXC launcher: cannot locate required Windows platform directory: HRESULT 0x80070003`. The updated core exposes the missing SystemDrive directly.
- Related report: #54157. This report adds the post-update direct-local-versus-fresh-DOT comparison and the explicit missing-host-variable diagnostic.
- #54027 addresses Windows startup/MXC environment handling. #54069 specifically preserves SYSTEMDRIVE and LOCALAPPDATA during remote MCP environment filtering: https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/54069
- Please verify that the hosted DOT-to-Windows launch route preserves the **Windows executor's own** SYSTEMDRIVE and LOCALAPPDATA before node_repl/MXC startup. The public merged fix does not establish that it is deployed or effective on this exact route.
- The failing test was observed without runtime patches, persistent environment edits, or sandbox changes. Private paths, account details, session IDs and raw logs are omitted.

Submitted by Codex with the account owner's authorization.

items.title: Standalone Unix updater reports success when curl fails (`curl | sh` masks the exit status); Windows path is unaffected

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

codex-cli 0.162.1

### What platform is your computer?

macOS (Darwin 27.0.0). Windows 10 22H2 (19045) was also tested for comparison.

### What issue are you seeing?

The standalone **Unix** updater prints `🎉 Update ran successfully! Please restart Codex.` even when `curl` fails and nothing is installed:

```text
Updating Codex via `sh -c 'curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh | CODEX_NON_INTERACTIVE=1 sh'`...
curl: (28) Failed to connect to chatgpt.com port 443 after 150008 ms: Couldn't connect to server

🎉 Update ran successfully! Please restart Codex.
```

This has been reported for individual symptoms in #19421 (curl 403) and #42021 (curl connect failure). This issue pins down the root cause, shows it only affects the Unix path, and proposes a fix.

#### Root cause

As of `6b99197`:

- `codex-rs/tui/src/update_action.rs` L55-61: `UpdateAction::StandaloneUnix` runs `sh -c "curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh | CODEX_NON_INTERACTIVE=1 sh"`.
- `codex-rs/cli/src/main.rs` L851-854: success is decided only by `status.success()` of that process.

POSIX `sh` has no `pipefail` by default, so the pipeline's exit status is that of the **last** command. When `curl` fails, the trailing `sh` reads empty stdin, runs nothing, and exits `0`.

`install.sh` itself handles errors correctly (`set -eu` plus explicit `exit 1`). The problem is only the `curl | sh` wrapper.

#### Unix reproduction (macOS, no Codex needed)

| Command | curl error | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `sh -c 'curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 2 https://10.255.255.1/x \| sh'` | `(28)` timeout | **0** ❌ |
| `sh -c 'curl -fsSL https://httpbin.org/status/404 \| sh'` | `(56)` HTTP 404 | **0** ❌ |
| `bash -o pipefail -c 'curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 2 https://10.255.255.1/x \| sh'` | `(28)` | **28** ✅ |

#### Windows is not affected (verified)

`UpdateAction::StandaloneWindows` runs `powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -c '$env:CODEX_NON_INTERACTIVE=1; irm https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.ps1 | iex'`. With `-Command`, PowerShell's exit code reflects `$?` of the last statement. A failing `irm` is a terminating error, so the process exits `1`. `install.ps1` also sets `$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"`, so a `throw` inside the script propagates the same way.

These results come from running the same `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass -c '<…> | iex'` shape on Windows 10 22H2:

| Case | Windows PowerShell 5.1.19041 | PowerShell 7 (`pwsh`) |
|---|---|---|
| `irm` connection refused (`https://127.0.0.1:9/…`) | exit **1** ✅ | exit **1** ✅ |
| `irm` connect timeout (`https://10.255.255.1/…`) | exit **1** ✅ | exit **1** ✅ |
| `irm` HTTP 404 | exit **1** ✅ | exit **1** ✅ |
| Script piped to `iex` throws | exit **1** ✅ | exit **1** ✅ |
| Control: script succeeds | exit 0 | exit 0 |

So only `StandaloneUnix` reports a false success.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Use a standalone (`install.sh`) install of Codex on macOS/Linux.
2. Make `https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh` unreachable (offline, firewall, proxy returning 403, etc.).
3. Accept the update prompt.
4. `curl` prints an error, but Codex still prints `🎉 Update ran successfully! Please restart Codex.`

### What is the expected behavior?

When the install script cannot be downloaded, the updater should report a failure (`… failed with status …`), and it should not tell the user to restart.

### Additional information

**Suggested fix:** download to a temp file first and execute it only if `curl` succeeded. This doesn't depend on `pipefail` support in `/bin/sh`:

```rust
UpdateAction::StandaloneUnix => (
    "sh",
    &[
        "-c",
        r#"tmp="$(mktemp)" || exit 1; trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT; curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh -o "$tmp" && CODEX_NON_INTERACTIVE=1 sh "$tmp""#,
    ],
),
```

Checked locally on macOS: a curl timeout exits 28, HTTP 404 exits 56, an installer that exits 3 propagates 3, and a successful installer exits 0.

As a side benefit, this also stops a connection that drops mid-transfer from running a truncated `install.sh`. With `curl | sh`, `sh` runs top-level statements as they stream in, and `install.sh` has no `main "$@"` wrapper at the end.

`set -o pipefail` would also work where it is supported, but `/bin/sh` does not support it on every platform.

The user-facing hint in the "Update available!" banner (`Run sh -c 'curl … | CODEX_NON_INTERACTIVE=1 sh' to update.`) uses the same command string, so it would pick up the fix automatically via `command_str()`.

Related: #19421, #42021

and list open tabs without modifying any tab or webpage.

items.body:
# Windows PowerShell safety heuristic flags UseShellExecute=false when unrelated loopback URL text is present

Codex CLI: 0.162.0-alpha.2 on Windows. Approval policy: never. Filesystem access: unrestricted. No local .rules files were found in the inspected user/project layers.

The Windows command classifier in tag rust-v0.162.0-alpha.2 flattens PowerShell script text using shlex. In `is_dangerous_powershell_words`, an HTTP/HTTPS URL anywhere in the token list combined with any token containing the substring `shellexecute` produces a dangerous match. This also matches the defensive assignment `.UseShellExecute = $false`, without requiring a ShellExecute call or process launch.

This is an inert, invented text example for static inspection; do not execute it to collect credentials or operate any device:

```powershell
$p = New-Object System.Diagnostics.ProcessStartInfo
$p.UseShellExecute = $false
$u = 'http://127.0.0.1:9/'
'inert text only'
```

The source branch at lines38–64 is sufficient to flag this text. The exec-policy fallback maps the dangerous match to Forbidden when approvals are never, then renders DangerousCommandMatch::Other as `blocked by policy`.

Observed wrapper output in a real authorized local development workflow:

```text
exec_command failed: CreateProcess { message: "Rejected(\"`<REDACTED_COMMAND>` rejected: blocked by policy\")" }
```

A separate attempted local diagnostic that only placed invented examples inside Python string literals was also rejected before process creation. Its diagnostic comparisons did not execute. The original command was not replayed, and no safety policy was disabled or overridden. Static PowerShell ParseInput on the original command reported zero top-level syntax errors. Those facts do not establish end-to-end authorization for that original action.

Please fix the classifier to distinguish setting UseShellExecute to false and inert data from actual URL-bearing ShellExecute operations, while retaining checks for real ShellExecute/Start-Process/browser launches and dangerous deletion. Suggested regression coverage: false assignment plus unrelated loopback URL; the same source text inside an inert Python string; actual ShellExecute URL invocation; Start-Process URL; forced deletion. An upgrade should only be recommended after the false-positive case and true-positive controls are verified.

Public source references:

- https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.0-alpha.2/codex-rs/shell-command/src/command_safety/windows_dangerous_commands.rs#L38
- https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.0-alpha.2/codex-rs/core/src/exec_policy.rs#L799

This report deliberately excludes project source, original command, session IDs, accounts, devices, credentials and private logs. It does not request a broad allowlist or a review bypass.


Related existing report: #47213. This report adds version-matched 0.162.0-alpha.2 source inspection and a refusal of a diagnostic containing only inert Python string examples; no candidate binary or policy modification was deployed.

- MacBook Air (Mac16,12), Apple M4 (4P + 6E), **16 GB RAM, fanless / passive cooling**

### What issue are you seeing?

Codex Desktop helper processes accumulate without bound while the app is idle, and never get reaped. On a 16 GB machine this saturates swap and drives sustained `WindowServer` CPU, which makes the whole system unusable (multi-second typing latency) and causes the machine to run hot.

This is reported against a **fanless** MacBook Air, where there is no thermal headroom to absorb the load.

#### Measured state (2026-10-15 21:14 EDT, uptime 5 days)

| Metric | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `ChatGPT.app` processes | **85** |
| `Codex (Renderer)` processes | **25** |
| MCP / Computer Use helper processes | **84** |
| Zombie (`<defunct>`) children | 2 |
| Physical memory | 15 GB used / 16 GB — **91 MB unused** |
| Compressor | 6603 MB |
| Swap | **18346 MB / 19456 MB (94%)** |
| `WindowServer` CPU | **37.5%** (sampled 51–70% earlier the same day) |
| `WindowServer` cumulative CPU | **566 minutes** (9.4 hours) |
| Displays | built-in only, 2560×1664, **no external display** |

`WindowServer` at 37–70% CPU with a single built-in display and no external monitor is anomalous; a healthy system sits in the 2–8% range. Per [#24185](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/24185), this appears to be driven by the Electron renderer/GPU layer rather than by memory pressure alone.

#### The leak regrows: direct measurement

This machine had a clean state 2 days before the above snapshot. I terminated **57** stale MCP helper processes (`node` / `npm exec` / `uv` / `python`, all children of the bundled `codex` app-server). Within **under 2 days**, with no unusual workload, the count regrew to **84**. Process counts on the ChatGPT side went 73 → 81 → 85 across three samples over the same period.

This is consistent with [#16256](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/16256) (MCP child trees are never reaped when a session ends), but the measurement here shows the regrowth rate on an **idle** machine, which I did not see quantified elsewhere.

#### `SkyComputerUseService` runs indefinitely

```
92018  08:15:20  16.6% CPU   /Users/<user>/.codex/computer-use/Codex Computer Use.app/Contents/MacOS/SkyComputerUseService
```

A single `SkyComputerUseService` instance had been running for **8h15m**, holding 16.6% CPU, alongside `/usr/libexec/replayd` at 3.6%. I did not invoke Computer Use during this window.

#### `~/.codex/config.toml` matches the leak variant in #43471

```toml
notify = ["/Users/<user>/.codex/computer-use/Codex Computer Use.app/Contents/SharedSupport/SkyComputerUseClient.app/Contents/MacOS/SkyComputerUseClient", "turn-ended"]

[plugins."unified-computer-use@openai-bundled"]

[plugins."computer-use@openai-bundled"]

[mcp_servers.computer-use]
command = "./Codex Computer Use.app/Contents/SharedSupport/SkyComputerUseClient.app/Contents/MacOS/SkyComputerUseClient"
args = ["mcp"]
```

Both Computer Use plugin variants are enabled simultaneously, which may relate to [#38307](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/38307). There are 12 `[mcp_servers.*]` entries configured (`excalidraw`, `lens`, `chrome-devtools`, `openaiDeveloperDocs`, `grafana`, `node_repl`, `computer-use`, `agent-hub`, …), so each leaked session tree multiplies by that count.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Install ChatGPT Desktop with Codex on macOS Apple Silicon (reproduced on 16 GB, fanless M4 MacBook Air).
2. Keep the Computer Use MCP server configured as shown above. Do **not** actively use Computer Use.
3. Leave the app running. Lock the screen or leave it idle.
4. Periodically sample:

```bash
# ChatGPT process family size
ps -Ao comm | grep -c 'ChatGPT.app'

# renderer count and summed RSS
ps -Ao rss,comm | grep 'Codex (Renderer)' | awk '{s+=$1} END {printf "%d procs, %.2f GiB\n", NR, s/1048576}'

# MCP / Computer Use helpers
ps -Ao args | grep -cE 'mcp-server|uvx|npm exec|SkyComputerUseClient'

# WindowServer CPU and cumulative time
ps -o pid,time,pcpu,comm -p $(pgrep -x WindowServer)

# memory pressure
top -l 1 -stats pid,command,mem | grep PhysMem
sysctl -n vm.swapusage

# leaked Children
ps -Ao pid,etime,pcpu,rss,comm | grep -i SkyComputerUse

# zombies
ps -Ao pid,stat,comm | awk '$2 ~ /^Z/'
```

5. Observe helper and renderer counts growing monotonically, swap climbing toward the ceiling, and `WindowServer` CPU rising with them. Terminating the helpers only resets the counter temporarily — they regrow.

**Expected:** helper and renderer counts stay bounded; a background app-server that received no turns holds roughly constant memory; idle Computer Use helpers exit or are reused rather than respawned.

**Actual:** counts grow without bound until swap saturates and `WindowServer` starves, degrading the entire system rather than just the app.

### What is the expected behavior?

- Helper and renderer process counts should remain bounded and correlate with actual open windows/sessions.
- MCP and Computer Use child trees should be reaped when their owning session ends.
- An idle app-server should not grow memory or spawn processes on a timer.
- `WindowServer` CPU should stay in the normal low-single-digit range for a single built-in display.

### Additional information

Searching before filing, I found these related reports. This issue is not a duplicate of any single one — it is the combined footprint on a memory-constrained, fanless machine, with the regrowth rate quantified:

- [#24185](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/24185) — sustained high CPU/GPU/WindowServer load and heating (open)
- [#53562](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/53562) — dozens of renderers retained with one window (open, filed 2026-10-13)
- [#43471](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/43471) — idle app-server leaks `SkyComputerUseClient` helpers, 6.4 GB RSS, two kernel panics (open)
- [#50514](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/50514) — recurring desktop slowdown, 19.79 GiB across 126 processes (open)
- [#26415](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/26415) — `SkyComputerUseService` spins at high CPU (closed)
- [#16256](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/16256) — MCP child processes never terminated (closed as duplicate)
- [#37249](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/37249) — zombie child processes until the process limit is hit (closed as duplicate)
- [#20313](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/20313) — `replayd` driven to 100% CPU
- [#25036](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/25036) — overheating when the app is in the foreground (M-series)
- [#38307](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/38307) — duplicate Computer Use services from two profiles

**Impact.** The machine becomes unusable roughly every 4–5 days of uptime: swap reaches 94%+, `WindowServer` climbs to 50–70%, and typing lag becomes multi-second. Because the MacBook Air is fanless, the sustained load also causes the chassis to get hot and the system to throttle (`kernel_task` observed at 63% CPU). The only reliable recovery is a full reboot or quitting ChatGPT, neither of which is acceptable as a routine workaround.

**Workarounds that do not work.** Launching with `--force-prefers-reduced-motion` had no effect, per #24185. `--disable-gpu --disable-gpu-compositing` was inconclusive. Manually killing helpers only resets the counter; the count regrew from 57 to 84 in under 2 days here.

**Not attached.** No session transcripts, prompts, account identifiers, repository contents, or screenshots. Paths are redacted to `/Users/<user>/`.
