items.title: Windows Computer Use: confirmed Korean UIA document-role failure and numeric ControlType fix

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
## Summary

On Korean Windows (`ko-KR`), an actual Codex Computer Use call against Chrome failed with `could not determine the current browser URL on Windows`, even though the browser's UI Automation document element exposed a nonempty URL value.

Live native observation identified the failing predicate: the helper compared the localized document role `문서` with the fixed English string `document`. Replacing only that predicate with a successful numeric `CachedControlType == UIA_DocumentControlTypeId` check restored actual screenshot and accessibility requests.

Related report: #53026. This report collects the Korean runtime reproduction, the causal before/after evidence, and the published repair tool in one place. The same evidence was initially added in [this comment](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/53026#issuecomment-6205535513).

## Environment observed on 2026-10-16

| Component | Observed version / identity |
| --- | --- |
| Codex installed Windows MSIX | `26.1007.9446.0` |
| Windows | x64, build `26100.9711` (24H2) |
| Windows UI culture | `ko-KR` |
| Computer Use plugin | `26.1007.71326` |
| `@oai/sky` | `0.7.7` |
| Chrome | `155.0.8059.79` |

The affected component was the bundled `@oai/sky/bin/windows/codex-computer-use.exe` native helper.

## Reproduction and actual behavior

1. Use the affected Codex Windows installation with Korean UI Automation document-role names and an open Chrome window.
2. Obtain that window with the documented `@oai/sky` API. Window lookup itself succeeds.
3. Ensure the window is not minimized, then request its state:

```js
await sky.get_window_state({
  window,
  include_screenshot: true,
  include_text: true,
});
```

The actual state request fails with the error containing:

```text
could not determine the current browser URL on Windows
```

The diagnostic calls did not navigate the page. The error occurred after successful window lookup, within the native state-capture path.

## Expected behavior

A UI Automation Document element should be recognized by its numeric ControlType, regardless of its localized display name. An eligible `RootWebArea` with a successfully read, nonempty URL value should support the normal Chrome state request in Korean as it does in English.

## Live evidence at the failing predicate

The initial observation recorded native getter results and comparisons without replacing their arguments or results.

| Property / operation | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Numeric UIA ControlType | `50030` (`UIA_DocumentControlTypeId`) |
| `CachedLocalizedControlType` | `문서` |
| `CachedAutomationId` | `RootWebArea` |
| Current value lookup | HRESULT `0`; nonempty value |
| Cached value lookup | HRESULT `0`; nonempty value |
| Document-role comparison | `문서` compared with ASCII `document`: false |
| URL candidate after visiting the element | Absent |
| Native URL-result discriminator | `0x8000000000000002` |

The mismatch appeared in 22 RootWebArea comparisons during 11 internal state captures within a five-second observation interval. These are internal capture counts, not 11 separate tool requests.

The native helper's resulting error propagates through the Computer Use response. The localized display name is being used as a semantic identifier in the URL-candidate selector.

## Narrow correction and causal validation

```text
Before: localized_role.eq_ignore_ascii_case("document")
After:  successful CachedControlType read
        AND CachedControlType == UIA_DocumentControlTypeId  // 50030
```

For causal validation, only this predicate was changed in the installed native helper: one existing 42-byte instruction region, with 36 bytes differing. Reconstructing the original region reproduced the original whole-file SHA-256, establishing that every byte outside that region was identical.

A failed numeric-property getter or a non-Document ControlType follows the existing non-candidate path. Subsequent RootWebArea matching and nonempty-value selection remain intact.

This was a local binary-level repair, not a build from upstream native source.

## Actual Computer Use results after the correction

The documented API was called against the same Chrome window after the predicate change:

| Request | Actual result |
| --- | --- |
| Screenshot + accessibility | Success: one 1920 x 1032 screenshot and a 48,951-character accessibility tree |
| Accessibility only | Success: accessibility tree returned |
| Screenshot only | Success: one screenshot returned |

None of these three calls returned the URL-detection error. An initial post-change request reported a separate minimized-window condition; `activate_window`, followed by refreshing the window with `get_window`, resolved that condition before the three successful requests above.

The results establish the cause and recovery for this observed Korean Chrome environment. They do not establish every possible cause of the same error text, nor do they constitute coverage of click/type operations or every locale.

## Published repair code

- [Repair tool and usage](https://github.com/heelee912/codex/tree/fix/windows-cua-document-control-type/tools/windows-cua-document-fix)
- [Exact commit: 95ee61d](https://github.com/heelee912/codex/commit/95ee61db4a387944889edc9a5b6e97272c8fca9d)

The fork adds a Python standard-library tool and a README. It supports read-only inspection, applying the exact predicate correction, and restoring the original bytes. It accepts only these two complete helper hashes:

```text
Original: d36ae6626bdced7ae07935d1a91be14425e8f6ce7c9b5c69f2d8d7df0c130d83
Repaired: c9b9981288951976c36b4c8febc8c2e21b53dfe9bab66f299c11f51592145855
```

Apply/readback, exact restoration, repeated apply/restore, rejection of an exclusively opened target, and rejection of an unknown hash were checked on a temporary file copy. The copy was removed; those packaging checks did not modify the installed helper.

The native helper implementation was absent from the inspected public repository tree at `6b991972c5b539198dcea9bac4fc14e57559c3af`. Consequently, the published code is a version-bound local repair tool. It is not an upstream native-source fix or a rebuilt Codex app. No OpenAI executable is included. Editing the helper changes its Authenticode result to `HashMismatch`; exact restoration reconstructs the original file.

## Requested upstream resolution

Please replace the localized document-kind comparison with a successful numeric `CachedControlType == UIA_DocumentControlTypeId` check in the native Windows Computer Use implementation, and ship the change in an official app/runtime update. Please link the maintainer PR or tracked internal fix here.

Suggested focused regression coverage:

1. Document ControlType `50030` with display names such as `문서`, `document`, and another translated name selects the same eligible RootWebArea URL candidate.
2. A different ControlType is not classified as Document merely because its display name is `document`.
3. A failed getter does not consume an uninitialized numeric property value.
4. Screenshot-only, accessibility-only, and combined requests succeed against the same eligible Chrome window on Korean Windows.

The local tool performs a one-time repair and does not watch or patch later app updates. The requested official source correction would be delivered through normal app/runtime updates.

## Community write-up

The repair tool and its actual validation results are also shared in [Show and tell #54474](https://github.com/openai/codex/discussions/54474).

items.title: [Windows Desktop] Direct user approval becomes untrusted after history restoration (history_missing_checkpoint)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

items.body:
## Summary

In a long-running Codex Desktop chat, a direct human approval for a precisely scoped update was present in the review transcript but was not retained as a trusted user instruction. Automatic review assigned `user_authorization=unknown` and denied the operation because the apparent authorization existed only in untrusted quoted history.

This report describes an observed provenance/authorization mismatch. The internal implementation defect and causality are **not established**. No bypass or relaxation of safety review is requested.

## Environment

- Windows, x64; Codex Desktop.
- Locally observed desktop package version: `26.1007.9446.0`.
- Running Codex engine: `0.162.0-alpha.17.2`; the running app and PATH resolved to the same engine executable.
- Long-running chat originally created on engine `0.151.0-alpha.7.2`; current `history_mode=paginated`.
- Restricted workspace filesystem boundary and automatic approval reviewer remained enabled.

## Observed sequence

1. An operation was denied because authorization was not recognized.
2. The human then directly approved an exact, bounded two-cell update in their existing spreadsheet.
3. The next review input included that direct message as a `user:` transcript item, but not in `RETAINED USER INSTRUCTIONS`.
4. The reviewer again assigned `user_authorization=unknown` and denied the operation, explaining that authorization appeared only in untrusted quoted history.
5. A subsequent structured confirmation card describing the same two-cell scope received the human's affirmative answer. The normal connector and safety review then returned `user_authorization=high` / `outcome=allow`. Readback confirmed that only the two intended cells changed.

Step 5 recovered that individual operation; it did not repair the provenance-restoration problem. Requiring repeated confirmation cards adds user effort and is not the requested permanent solution.

This is a historical observed sequence, **not a clean minimal or deterministic reproducer**. No fresh production mutation was performed to reproduce the bug for this report.

## Sanitized diagnostic observations

The locally retained metadata on the actual direct human message contained:

```json
{"client_authored":false,"mcp_attribution":{"status":"attribution_error","error_reason":"restored_error_unknown"}}
```

Affected review-input metadata contained:

```json
{"mcp_attribution":{"status":"attribution_error","error_reason":"history_missing_checkpoint"},"guardian_retained_omissions":{"user_instructions":true,"assistant_context":true}}
```

The direct approval text was present in the quoted transcript while absent from retained user instructions. This appears relevant to the reviewer's stated denial reason, but does not establish which persistence/restoration component failed.

A provenance error was already persisted by October 1, before a later notification-policy-only change. The same checkpoint error also appeared in earlier **allowed** assessments. Therefore, its presence alone is not sufficient to predict denial, and there is no evidence that the notification change introduced the error.

## Independent read-only checks

- The target JSONL parsed without errors.
- The official `doctor` diagnostic, run under the normal user outside the restricted diagnostic subprocess, reported database integrity `ok` for state, thread history, logs, goals, memories, and queue.
- Initial SQLite open/code14 failures inside the restricted subprocess were not reproduced under the normal user and were treated as permission artifacts, not corruption.
- `migrate-rollouts --thread <redacted> --json`, **without `--apply`**, returned `already_paginated` and `bytes_processed=0`.
- No standalone attribution/checkpoint table was found in the inspected thread-history schema. No supported checkpoint-regeneration command was found in the installed doctor/debug/migrate-rollouts help. This is a limited local observation, not proof that no internal recovery exists.
- The desktop composer did not offer `/approve`; filtering for it displayed the localized equivalent of “No commands.”
- No history, trust metadata, database records, or security configuration were modified.

## Expected behavior / requested investigation

Please investigate whether pagination, compaction, resume, or review-context retention can cause a newly supplied, host-authored human instruction to lose its verifiable provenance.

A new direct human grant should remain distinguishable from assistant quotations and tool-origin content and should be matched to the exact proposed action. The reviewer should still independently assess risk and reject unauthorized operations. We are not requesting unconditional approval.

Please provide a supported recovery for affected existing chats that does not forge trust metadata, weaken safety settings, or require repeated approval cards, or a product fix if appropriate.

Suggested regression cases:

1. Resume a long paginated chat when an older attribution checkpoint is unavailable; preserve provenance of a new direct human grant.
2. Continue to reject assistant/tool quotations falsely claiming human approval.
3. Carry a direct human grant after a denial into the next exact-action assessment.
4. Keep notification policy independent of authorization scope and provenance.

## Possibly related report

#49609 mentions `history_missing_checkpoint` in a long-running desktop chat, but concerns invisible replies/compaction on macOS rather than lost authorization. A common root cause is **not** established.

## Privacy

This report contains only generalized technical symptoms, diagnostic field names, and version information. No business details, spreadsheet/email/account identifiers, local usernames or paths, session IDs, original conversation text, raw logs, credentials, screenshots, or attachments are included. Raw logs are not authorized for submission.

items.body:
## Summary
User-authorized diagnostic report for two unresolved Windows desktop / dot-delegated task failures. Please triage the cross-thread turn-parameter error and the Computer Use executor startup failure. These occur in the same workflow, but a common root cause has NOT been established.

Related reports:
- #54308 and #51679: AbsolutePathBuf / cloud task messaging
- #54153 and #53356: MXC platform-directory startup failure

This report adds a same-machine comparison between a working local task and a failing dot-delegated task, plus a failed post-restart cross-thread test.

## Environment
- Windows 11 25H2, build 26200.9711, x64
- Installed desktop package observed during diagnosis: 26.1007.9446.0
- Selected CLI: codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.17.2
- CUA runtime cache: cua_node/a9ba6825a525118c
- Selected CLI cache: bin/9614f1d9b40d9c4f/codex.exe
- Diagnostic date: 2026-10-16, Asia/Taipei
- Local task coordination works; affected dot-delegated task is reported as hostId durable with Windows local command execution.

## A. Cross-thread messaging rejected before a new turn starts
### Reproduction
1. From an existing local desktop task, call the official send_message_to_thread tool targeting an existing dot-delegated diagnostic task.
2. Send a minimal plain-text request to acknowledge receipt, with no file paths, attachments, model overrides, or requested actions.
3. Test with the returned durable host ID and also with hostId omitted.
4. User fully restarts the desktop app; repeat the minimal test.

### Actual
Both variants and the post-restart test return:
```
invalid turn/start params: AbsolutePathBuf deserialized without a base path
```
Matching desktop log:
```
method=turn/start
errorCode=-32602
failureReason=invalid_config
```

Reading the target's history still works. Readback after the post-restart test shows no acknowledgement/new receiving turn for our test. Another diagnostic message delivered by the dot's own cloud_threads route had previously succeeded; that is not evidence our local send_message_to_thread call succeeded.

The returned cwd has this REDACTED shape:
```
/tmp/codex-cloud-agent-<id>/app_servers/thread_service/workspace/C:\Users\<user>\Documents\<workspace>\task
```
Read-only bundled-code inspection found that sendFollowUpMessage obtains cwd from conversation state (fallback "/") and uses it for workspaceRoots during resume. The exposed tool does not accept a cwd/workspaceRoots override.

This is evidence worth investigating, not proof that this cwd is the precise offending field. Please identify which AbsolutePathBuf field fails and fix host-appropriate path serialization/base resolution. Do not require users to weaken permissions or edit task databases.

## B. Computer Use startup fails in the dot-delegated task
Official test:
```js
// separate calls
await cua_repl.js_reset();
await cua.getState();
```
(The reset is the tool named mcp__cua_repl.js_reset; getState is executed through mcp__cua_repl.js.)

Reset succeeds; getState fails before obtaining a screenshot:
```
node_repl kernel exited unexpectedly
MXC launcher: cannot locate required Windows platform directory: HRESULT 0x80070003
kernel_status: exited(code=1)
reason: stdout_eof
stream_error: null
```
Observed failure: 2026-10-16 08:45:15 Asia/Taipei. No mouse/keyboard test followed the failure.

### Same-machine differential probe
Using the same selected CLI, the official compatibility command:
```powershell
& $selectedCodex -c windows.sandbox=mxc sandbox --include-managed-config --permission-profile :workspace -- cmd.exe /d /c echo MXC_OK
```
- Local task: MXC_OK, exit 0.
- Dot-delegated task at 2026-10-16 08:52:41–08:52:42 Asia/Taipei: inner probe exit 1:
```
Error: failed to prepare MXC sandbox: native MXC is unavailable on this executor
```
The enclosing PowerShell script exits 0; this must not be mistaken for MXC success.

Within the delegated task:
- SHGetKnownFolderPath for ProgramFiles, ProgramFilesX86, and ProgramData returns HRESULT 0 and existing paths.
- SystemRoot, WINDIR, TEMP, TMP, LOCALAPPDATA, ProgramFiles, ProgramFiles(x86), ProgramData all point to existing locations.
- TEMP/TMP/LOCALAPPDATA are redirected under:
  %LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages\sandbox.{<id>}\AC (Temp for TEMP/TMP)
- CLI startup additionally reports os error 5 while attempting its own stale arg0 cleanup / PATH aliases under %USERPROFILE%\.codex\tmp\arg0.
- No retry to bypass those restrictions was performed.

The local task previously obtained a real Notepad screenshot using its supported node_repl + @oai/sky route. This does not demonstrate that the delegated task's cua_repl is functional.
The inspected unified-computer-use manifest exposes CUA_REPL_ENABLED_SURFACES=browser, so fixing kernel initialization alone must not be assumed to enable native desktop screenshots.

## Requested fixes / acceptance
1. Fix cross-thread turn/start parameter/path handling for cloud-coordinated Windows tasks; verify with an acknowledgement actually recorded in the receiving task.
2. Diagnose the exact failed platform-directory lookup in the delegated CUA launch context, including executor/sandbox nesting and environment propagation. The compatibility probe inside that executor is a different launch context from the failing CUA kernel and does not alone prove the cause.
3. Restore supported Computer Use initialization in that task type, and clarify native-desktop capability availability. Verify an actual screenshot from the affected delegated task, not from a separate working local task.
4. Provide actionable diagnostics naming the failed path/API rather than the generic directory error.

## Privacy and limits
No credentials, private thread IDs, user-specific absolute paths, full logs, business records, or desktop screenshots are attached. No system/security/network settings, services, or app binaries were modified. Neither issue is claimed fixed. Additional private identifiers should be collected through official private support/feedback if needed.

## Follow-up: cross-thread failure narrowed, still unresolved (2026-10-16)

A further authorized screenshot-test message failed at 09:07:53 Asia/Taipei (01:07:53 UTC), before a receiving turn started. The target remains readable through the official read_thread tool and has no new receiving turn for this request.

Immediately before the failure, the desktop log recorded:
```text
requestRuntimeWorkspaceRootCount=0
requestSandboxPolicyType=workspaceWrite
requestSandboxWritableRootCount=1
requestPermissionProfile=null
useAppServerPermissionDefault=false
method=turn/start
errorCode=-32602
failureReason=invalid_config
invalid turn/start params: AbsolutePathBuf deserialized without a base path
```

Together with the mixed-platform cwd shape in section A, the inherited sandbox writable-root field is a candidate for investigation. Its raw value is not present in the inspected log, so neither the exact offending path nor the failing field is confirmed. Related field-level analysis: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/54262#issuecomment-6204183151. That report logs useAppServerPermissionDefault=true; our failing request logs false, so these are not identical configurations.

The currently exposed cross-thread messaging tool has no cwd, workspaceRoots, or sandbox writable-root override. We have not changed task databases, patched application binaries, or relaxed sandbox permissions to force delivery. Please provide a supported repair that preserves the existing conversation and effective restrictions.

The cross-thread error remains unresolved, and the affected delegated task has not produced the requested screenshot. A successful screenshot in a separate local task must not count as acceptance. Please verify both actual message receipt in the affected task and its own supported screenshot capability after repair.

items.title: [macOS 26.1007.71326] Renderer V8 footprint reaches 4.5G; replacing window releases it without app restart — request retained-object diagnosis and durable fix

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using?

ChatGPT/Codex Desktop **26.1007.71326 (build 20398)**; bundled **codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.17.2**; Codex Framework / Chromium **155.0.8059.40**. This is the macOS desktop renderer, not a CLI-only memory report.

### Platform

Apple silicon, **16 GiB RAM**, **macOS 26.6.2 (25G83)**. Production packaged build; startup diagnostics report developer tools, inspect element and debug menu disabled. Subscription tier omitted from this public report.

### Issue and impact

The user reports that recently, sustained Codex use for approximately two hours repeatedly makes the whole Mac sluggish or unresponsive. Exiting the application sometimes makes reopening difficult. Earlier retained evidence also contains memory-pressure incidents, so a recent regression's precise start date has **not** been established.

During investigation, a **single desktop renderer's physical footprint rose from roughly 1.2G to 4.5G** while navigating and archiving conversations. It later partially reclaimed memory without an application restart, but retained approximately 1.3–1.5G for hours. Replacing the old window while leaving the desktop main process and app-server running terminated that renderer and established a fresh renderer at approximately 607M.

This is a request for **object-level attribution and a durable fix**, not a request to treat periodic window replacement, deleting history, or restarting the application as the solution. **There is no heap snapshot proving a particular retaining object or a leak.**

The 4.5G peak occurred during diagnostic navigation/archive activity. It must not be presented as a proven reproduction of every earlier whole-machine freeze.

### Measured renderer memory

All times below are **2026-10-16, UTC+08:00**. Values preserve `vmmap -summary`'s rounded M/G units; these are not exact byte counts.

| Time | Renderer physical footprint | Tag 255 resident | Tag 255 swapped/compressed column | Tag 253 resident |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 00:52:21 | 4.1G | 3.2G | 318.3M | 452.8M |
| 00:53:21 | **4.5G** | 2.5G | 1.3G | 388.4M |
| 00:53:51 | 2.8G | 2.5G | 156.6M | 547.3M |
| 08:24 | 1.5G | about 1.0G | 143.8M | 216.0M |

The matching upstream Chromium version's [`PageTag` definition](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/155.0.8059.40/base/allocator/partition_allocator/src/partition_alloc/page_allocator.h) identifies **255 as V8 heap pages** and **253 as PartitionAlloc**. This supports allocation-category attribution; it does not identify live JS objects, strings, arrays, retainers, or prove that all committed heap pages contain live objects. A patched binary's tag assignment was not independently disassembled.

Resident, swapped/compressed, and footprint accounting must not be summed as if they were unique physical RAM. Huge virtual reservations such as 1.4T were not treated as RAM consumption. `vmmap` warned it could not fully introspect the Chromium PartitionAlloc malloc zone.

### Activity during the growth window

In the retained **00:47:00–00:53:50** desktop log window, requests attributable to the visible frontend (`originWebcontentsId=1`) included:

- **1,098** `thread/attachment/list` responses for **1,068 distinct thread IDs**. These are worktree/PR association metadata, **not** 1,068 downloaded image attachments or complete conversation histories.
- **519** `thread/archive` requests involving **402 distinct threads**. The first successful archive for each was followed by **117 duplicate attempts** returning missing-rollout errors. This is not 117 independent first-attempt failures.
- **48** navigation spans: 6 success, 42 aborted with `navigation_away`.
- **47** hydration spans: 5 success, **42 aborted** with `hydration_canceled`.
- The 42 aborted hydration spans all recorded writable-roots and metadata readiness, but none recorded `history_ready` or `runtime_resume_started`. Durations were approximately **388–3747 ms**. This does not establish that their underlying I/O was fully canceled or that no response data ever arrived.
- An inventory saved before user deletion could match **46 of 47** resume-request thread IDs. **45 matched conversations had at most 20 canonical items**. No matched inventory contained `imageGeneration`; one conversation contained 14 `imageView` items. Pre-existing caches and the unmatched conversation are not covered by this inventory.
- Among responses recorded in this window, metadata requests were fast (`thread/attachment/list` p95 about 3 ms, max 21 ms); `thread/items/list` max 31 ms; `thread/turns/list` max 157 ms; five completed `thread/resume` responses had max 292 ms. Reconstructed overlapping intervals from **completed, logged responses only** peaked at five. This excludes outstanding/unlogged/window-crossing work and is not a bound on all application concurrency or response processing.

The exact OS renderer PID to webContentsId mapping was not available through the supported tools. Activity and renderer growth are correlated, not a proven object-retention chain.

A subsequent background archive phase (**00:59:58–01:05:52**) produced more archive/read requests without recreating the 4.5G peak. It is an imperfect comparison because navigation and payloads were not controlled. The background task beginning at 00:53:50 cannot cause the peak already measured at 00:53:21.

### Reclamation and window-lifecycle evidence

1. Read-only inspection of the installed code shows separate frontend page retention (up to 10 pages, about 10-minute TTL) and eligible inactive owner-conversation retention (about 3 hours, plus a count-based policy). Active views, stream followers, runtime state and pending interaction conditions can exclude a conversation from reclamation. These are not universal byte limits.
2. One actual conversation changed to inactive at **00:50:19.654** and logged successful `inactive_thread_unsubscribed` at **03:50:19.973**, a difference of **10,800.319 seconds**. Thus this cleanup mechanism really runs in at least some cases.
3. Around that event the app-server footprint declined from 335.0M to 247.2M; a five-process tool-runtime cohort also ended shortly afterward. The cohort was not conclusively mapped to that conversation, so its ownership/cause of termination is not asserted. The main renderer still retained about 1.3G.
4. Archive/delete code has invalidation and cleanup paths. History application code also checks whether its resume attempt and history references remain current. **This report does not claim that cleanup is entirely missing, that every aborted request writes stale data back, or that every unsubscribe leaks.**
5. On macOS, read-only inspection indicates closing the last primary window hides it. With another primary window open, the old window takes its normal close path. The user tested File > New Window, opened the same conversation there, then closed the old window.

**Measured replacement test:**

| Component | Before (08:25) | After (08:28–08:29) |
|---|---|---|
| Desktop main | same PID, 446.0M | **same PID**, 443.1M; uptime about 8h45m |
| Bundled app-server | same PID, 316.6M | **same PID**, 331.9M |
| Old peak renderer | 1.5G; lifetime peak 4.5G | **process exited** |
| Newly appearing main-sized renderer | absent | 606.6M; lifetime peak 902.7M |
| Existing secondary renderer | 580.1M | 669.0M |
| System pressure / used swap | normal / 26.81 MiB | normal / 26.81 MiB |

Several old secondary renderers also exited and several new ones appeared. Across adjacent minute samples, renderer RSS sums fell from 3208.2 to 2858.1 MiB, and bundle-path process RSS sums from 4502.1 to 4331.1 MiB. **These shared-page-sensitive RSS sums are not unique footprint totals.** Subtracting the new main-sized renderer's footprint from the old renderer's footprint would overstate a measured net application saving.

The user remained in the same conversation without restarting the desktop main process or app-server. This is a verified temporary way to release the old renderer, **not** a durable fix or proof of which JS objects account for its memory.

### Other checks and limits

- Nearly six hours of low-frequency overnight sampling before the user's return showed normal system pressure, falling swap (50.88 to 26.81 MiB), partial renderer reclamation, and eventually stable residual use. Hourly/half-hourly diagnostic turns caused some activity, so this was **not** a strictly idle experiment. The user resumed interaction at approximately 07:31 and replaced the window around 08:28; those stages must be analyzed separately.
- Current log database/WAL observations showed bounded reuse rather than indefinite WAL growth. TRACE writes were not anomalously high in the measured sample. Disk had about 263 GiB available; this incident is not a verified disk-full/swap-exhaustion crash.
- A broken ChatCut MCP executable configuration was independently confirmed and removed at the user's request around 07:34. There was a subsequent startup failure in an already running/prepared context, so complete runtime refresh is not asserted. Its repeated errors also occurred during renderer plateau/reclamation; no causal link to the 4.5G peak is established.
- The current diagnostic conversation had approximately **2.83 MiB of canonical JSON across 1,164 items** at 08:33, no image-generation/view items, and largest item 70,710 bytes. This excludes other window state and does not predict parsed/rendered heap size.
- `codex doctor` is an installation/runtime health check, not an object heap profile. A small memories database could not be opened at its original location, but an unchanged, no-WAL copy passed `quick_check`; it was **not** treated as proven corruption or rebuilt. No database corruption claim is made here.
- A special snapshot-query branch with `gcTime=Infinity` was inspected, but there is no runtime evidence that ordinary desktop conversation reads use it or that it retains the observed objects. It is not asserted as root cause.

### Requested investigation / durable outcome

Please provide a **supported way to collect renderer heap/GC diagnostics on this production macOS build**, ideally without requiring repeated application exit or window replacement, and investigate:

1. Object-type counts, retained sizes, dominator tree and paths to GC roots before growth, at peak, and after page/conversation eviction.
2. Conversation/turn arrays, query payloads and observers, hidden React Activity/page state, detached DOM, stream followers/subscriptions, canceled hydration promises/callbacks and derived rendering structures.
3. **Live V8 objects vs. unused but retained heap pages**, with GC-before/after measurements; native/PartitionAlloc and GPU attribution should remain separate.
4. OS PID/webContents/window mapping and whether multiple views retain or replicate unnecessary full state.
5. Lifecycle invalidation, cancellation, and byte-aware retention/pagination budgets appropriate for long tool-heavy conversations.

Expected result: bounded memory during sustained normal work and a permanent application-level fix where a retaining path is confirmed. The user does not consider periodic window recreation, clearing history or restarts an acceptable long-term solution.

### Related report and privacy

#54416 reports high main/renderer footprint on the same desktop build, but a different workload and OS-failure context. No identical root cause is assumed.

The tables and counts above are sanitized measured evidence. The user has authorized reporting this incident. Raw chats, original SQLite databases, credentials/configuration, personal filesystem paths, request/thread IDs, proprietary project contents and installed application source are **not uploaded publicly**. A local sanitized evidence bundle has been prepared; targeted further excerpts or diagnostic captures can be supplied once maintainers specify a supported collection method and the needed fields.

items.title: [Bug][Codex Goals][Cloud/Windows/Web] Failed to set goal on new no-attachment cloud thread while task executes

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: codex-web
labels.description: Issues related to Codex Web

labels.name: agent
labels.description: Issues related to the core agent loop

items.body:
## Summary / What issue are you seeing?

On **October 16, 2026**, using **Pursue Goal** in Codex on a **new Cloud conversation** backed by a **newly published Cloud environment** produces a red error toast:

    Не удалось установить цель
    (English: Failed to set goal)

However, the conversation simultaneously labels the prompt **"Отправлено в качестве цели" ("Submitted as goal")** and the cloud agent starts executing it. The read-only test task finishes successfully after **2 minutes 16 seconds**.

Thus the UI communicates both a **failure to set the persistent goal** and an apparently successful **goal-type submission**. It is unclear whether a durable goal exists, whether the prompt fell back to a normal task, or whether the client/server goal status diverged.

The user previously encountered the same Goal error in a separate research workspace, and reports that a fresh browser-window attempt also fails. Those additional observations are user reports, not independent backend traces.

**Important difference from prior reports:** the test used a newly created Cloud environment and a short read-only prompt **without file attachments**. No SSH forwarding, local attachments, large-context prompts, real trading activity, or special application code is required to see the error.

## Environment

| Field | Observed |
| --- | --- |
| Date | 2026-10-16, approximately 03:14–03:22 local time (UTC+03:00) |
| Subscription | ChatGPT Plus |
| Client / OS | Codex on Windows; similar failure also reported in a separate browser window |
| Exact Codex desktop build | Not yet collected; can be provided from About Codex |
| Browser name/version | Not independently verified |
| Model | GPT-6.1 Sol Ultra |
| Execution mode | Cloud |
| GitHub repository | Newly created private repository, name deliberately omitted |
| Cloud environment | Newly configured, tested, and successfully published |
| Python | 3.12.14 inside a local .venv in the cloud checkout |
| Packages verified | pytest, NumPy, pandas, SciPy, PyArrow, Matplotlib |
| Environment tests | 3/3 smoke checks passed; pip check passed |
| Connectivity confirmed | GitHub, public Pine documentation, PyPI and arXiv |
| Attached files | **None** |
| Goal storage/database logs | Not inspected; root cause unknown |

A previous environment-onboarding task finished in about **1 minute 40 seconds**, and the user received the explicit UI confirmation that the Cloud environment had been published. The environment and normal Cloud task execution are functional.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On a Windows machine, open Codex with ChatGPT Plus.
2. Create a new private GitHub repository with a few ordinary Markdown guidance files.
3. Create a **new Codex Cloud environment** tied to that repository. Run the environment setup checks and publish it.
4. Open a **new chat**, choose **Cloud**, and select the freshly published environment.
5. Select **GPT-6.1 Sol Ultra**.
6. Paste a short, read-only goal; **do not attach files**. Observed prompt, with project name replaced by a placeholder:

        Goal: Verify that <PROJECT> is ready for autonomous research.

        Read AGENTS.md, GOAL_PROMPT.md, and docs/RESEARCH_PROTOCOL.md.
        Verify repository access, Python environment, and the availability
        of the core research dependencies.

        Do not modify repository files, create commits, download datasets,
        or begin the actual research.

        Return a concise readiness report with any detected blockers.

7. Select the **Goal / Цель** composer mode (the Goal chip is visibly selected). The composer also shows the default/selected "Confirm for me" option.
8. Press Send.
9. Observe the red toast **"Не удалось установить цель"** at the top of the conversation.
10. Nevertheless, beneath the sent prompt, observe the **"Отправлено в качестве цели"** label and the agent's normal response. It begins performing the requested checks.
11. After approximately **2m16s**, observe a successful readiness report. The report verifies the repository checkout, Git HEAD, packages, Python and network access. No repository changes are made.

The user reports reproducing the Goal-setting problem in another project and a separate browser window as well; exact browser version and a browser trace are still outstanding.

## Expected behavior

- When Goal is selected, sending a prompt should **register/persist** the durable goal and show an unambiguous **active goal** state.
- The client should obtain a successful goal-write acknowledgment/readback before describing the goal as established.
- If goal registration fails but the regular turn is accepted, the UI should explicitly say **"Goal could not be saved; continuing as a normal cloud task"**, not simultaneously imply goal success and display a generic failure.
- Goal failures should expose a non-sensitive error category or correlation ID and a supported recovery path.
- A short no-attachment prompt against a healthy new Cloud workspace should not trigger this behavior.

## Actual behavior / evidence matrix

| Operation | Result | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Create and publish separate Cloud environment | PASS | Published-success UI |
| Run environment checks | PASS | Python, dependencies, 3 smoke tests |
| Start fresh Cloud chat with correct environment | PASS | Composer UI |
| Choose Goal mode | PASS visually | Goal chip in composer |
| Submit short no-attachment Goal | **FAIL to set Goal** | Red failure toast |
| Message marked "Submitted as goal" | YES | UI label |
| Cloud task starts running | PASS | Agent progress response |
| Cloud task completes | PASS, **2m16s** | Read-only readiness report |
| Durable goal actually exists and persists | **UNVERIFIED** | No goal-store inspection |
| Browser-window attempt | Reported failure | Browser diagnostics unavailable |
| SQLite state/migration hypothesis | **UNVERIFIED** | No DB inspection |

The task returned successful results: a clean Git working tree, remote and local HEAD aligned, Python 3.12.14, installed test/scientific dependencies, successful pip check and 3 smoke tests. This strongly suggests that Goal registration and basic Cloud execution take separate paths, but does **not** establish where goal registration fails.

## Impact

- Users cannot rely on Pursue Goal for long-running, multi-stage autonomous work, even when Cloud tasks execute normally.
- The contradictory error toast and "Submitted as goal" status make the actual Goal state impossible to determine from the interface.
- Repeated attempts across new projects, environments or browser windows consume user time and may consume task budget.
- The user has temporarily switched to ordinary Cloud tasks with GitHub checkpoint files while Goal is unavailable.

## Related issues and duplicate check

I checked existing reports before filing:

- **#24140** — Windows Desktop "Failed to set goal" and "Failed to clear goal"; **closed (duplicate)**.
- **#24282** — goal not inserted after thread title generation; **closed**.
- **#25407** — goal-store migration / thread_goals SQLite errors on an older build; **closed**.
- **#25455** — **open**, Windows-to-SSH with **local attachments**, ambiguous "Failed to set goal" while SSH task can still start.
- **#33443** — malformed local goals SQLite database, previously reported.

This report is **not necessarily a new root cause**. It documents a distinct, more minimal **Cloud + fresh environment + no attachments** repro, the UI's contradictory success/failure signals, and a separate-browser observation. In particular it does not require the SSH/local-attachment scenario of #25455.

No SQLite error was actually observed in this reproduction. DB migration/authentication/client-server desynchronization are **hypotheses only**, not diagnoses.

## Suggested investigation

1. Trace the complete lifecycle of a Goal request: UI selection -> thread creation/submission -> persistent goal-set RPC -> acknowledgment -> goal readback -> active Goal UI.
2. Check whether a task can be queued/run **before** goal persistence succeeds, and whether the app misleadingly labels it "Submitted as goal" after a failed write.
3. Compare current Goal behavior in **Windows desktop** and **web Cloud chat**; cover **no-attachment** prompts as well as attachment/SSH cases.
4. Look for request authorization, storage-migration, workspace/environment mapping or session synchronization errors, while keeping the root cause open until backed by logs.
5. Provide an actionable error code/correlation ID, or separate states for "turn submitted" vs. "goal persisted."
6. Add a regression test using a newly published Cloud environment and fresh thread, with a short read-only Goal prompt, verifying durable goal readback and UI state.

## Privacy and follow-up diagnostics

The user has screenshots showing the environment, selected Goal mode, error toast, the cloud agent running, and the final readiness report. They can provide **sanitized** screenshots and the exact app/browser versions as follow-up. If diagnostics include account details, workspace IDs, session IDs, OAuth information, local paths or logs, please request them through an appropriate private support channel.

No private repo names, keys, cookies, tokens, internal database contents or session identifiers are published in this issue.

This report is submitted at the user's request. They rely on Codex for engineering research and want to help OpenAI reproduce and fix the problem. Thanks for your work and for any debugging guidance.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using?
Exact desktop app version was not retrieved. The installed Computer Use skill bundle was 26.1007.71326. These are distinct version identifiers.

### What subscription do you have?
Not collected.

### What platform is your computer?
Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.19045.0. Google Chrome controlled through the ChatGPT browser extension, plus comparison with the built-in browser.

The extension displayed version 1.26.1005.11759 before the user ran Chrome's extension Update action. The post-update version was not independently verified.

### What issue are you seeing?
On Brandboom seller login, an authorized Google OAuth account chooser opens and is readable, but selecting an existing signed-in Google account through browser control repeatedly times out. This blocks the agent from completing sign-in without a manual account-selection click.

Observed Chrome error:
```text
Timed out after 2998ms waiting for CDP command Input.dispatchMouseEvent.
```

The semantic locator matched exactly one visible, enabled element:
```js
await googlePopup.playwright.getByRole("link", {
  name: "ACCOUNT DISPLAY NAME account@example.com",
  exact: true
}).click();
```
The account label above is a placeholder; no actual account identity is included.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?
1. Open https://manage.brandboom.com/ in a Chrome tab controlled by the desktop agent.
2. If authenticated, sign out using Brandboom's visible Logout control.
3. Click Continue with Google.
4. Discover the new Google account-chooser popup/tab using the documented Chrome tab APIs.
5. Read its accessibility/DOM state. The saved Google account is visible as a link.
6. Select that account through an accessibility click or semantic locator click.
7. Observe Input.dispatchMouseEvent timeout and no verified return to the authenticated Brandboom dashboard.

### What is the expected behavior?
The agent should be able to select the user-authorized existing Google account through the supported browser-control API, complete the OAuth callback, and verify the expected vendor account. Existing URL, permission, and authentication protections should remain enforced.

### Additional information
- Parent Brandboom tab interactions worked, including opening its account menu, Logout, reload, and Continue with Google.
- The Google popup could be discovered, read, and eventually captured in a screenshot.
- The account element was a visible DIV with role=link, tabindex=0, and nonzero geometry.
- Keyboard activation focused the account but did not produce verified sign-in.
- A screenshot-coordinate click returned without error, but did not establish successful sign-in; a subsequent popup read timed out on Page.getFrameTree.
- A later attempt to close an earlier popup reported that the tab was not part of the browser session. That alone does not establish the cause.
- Reloading the parent, opening a fresh popup, and explicitly calling browser.user.claimTab with the exact object from browser.user.openTabs did not resolve the semantic-click timeout.
- The user ran Chrome's extension Update action after a tool requested an update. The fresh test still failed; an actual version change was not verified.
- In the built-in browser comparison, Google also opened a separate native chooser. Windows accessibility could read it, but native input reported "coordinate input geometry is unavailable" and window capture timed out.
- The user manually selected the intended account in the built-in browser flow, after which the agent verified authenticated Brandboom access. Thus the account was usable.
- A later native Windows fallback stopped because it could not determine the current browser URL with sufficient confidence to enforce policy. The agent stopped; no bypass was attempted.

Related reports checked: #19373 (cross-origin iframe error on macOS), #40358 (general session-route/input timeouts on macOS), #40352 (Windows claim/get/new-tab hangs), and #43653 (JavaScript confirm handling). This report concerns a readable Google OAuth account chooser on Windows, with working parent-tab input and repeatable popup account-selection failure; the underlying cause remains unverified.

Please investigate popup target attachment/ownership and CDP input routing, and provide a supported recovery path.

No passwords, OAuth state/code URLs, private browser identifiers, screenshots with account identities, or customer records are included.

items.body:
## Summary

The user explicitly requested that the assistant report a serious loss of reliability in a long-running Codex desktop session. This report was drafted and submitted by the assistant at that request. The user says Codex normally works well for them, but that this day involved repeated errors, excessive work, and repeated corrections.

The concrete incident below is directly supported by the conversation and tool results. An exact count of all errors that day has not been audited.

## Environment

- Windows desktop, local repository and PowerShell.
- Bundled executable reports `codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.17.2`; this is not asserted to be the desktop UI version.
- Session turn metadata records `gpt-6-astra` throughout the available history. No model-selection change was found; a server-side model change or regression has not been established.
- Observed October 15, 2026, Pacific Time.
- Long-running task with substantial business rules and AGENTS.md instructions, including separate database-matching and website-deployment scopes.

## Concrete observed sequence

1. The user asked the assistant to resolve pending database catalog matches using rules already established in the conversation.
2. A multi-vintage pack could be represented by an existing catalog convention, with a separate six-component historical resolution. The assistant initially treated the absence of newer application handling as a matching blocker.
3. The assistant created one correct catalog entry but withheld the database link because it identified a separate My Cellar presentation/import problem.
4. It framed an application deployment as the prerequisite for finishing the match and asked for permission to deploy a narrow exclusion fix.
5. After the user questioned whether this was just adding a database link, a brief “yes” was interpreted as approval for the expanded deployment plan. The assistant started two previously stopped staging slots and began release preparation.
6. The user then repeatedly clarified that this was a quick database job and that nothing should be deployed to any website.
7. The assistant stopped release work before any code deployment, restored both staging slots to their original stopped state, and completed the database link. Live database verification showed the pending feed was empty.
8. The separate application issue was still unresolved when the database link was made. The assistant's explanation changed from treating it as a hard safety prerequisite to treating it as a separate follow-up. That inconsistency needs investigation; completing the original request does not establish that the downstream risk disappeared.

## Failures to investigate

- Scope expansion: a bounded database-matching task became application release preparation and cloud staging operations.
- Failure to apply an already established business rule promptly.
- Inconsistent reasoning about whether a downstream concern actually blocks the requested action.

items.body:
## Summary

Please track MSYS compatibility under the Windows MXC sandbox as a Codex functional regression, including Git operations that invoke MSYS-dependent helpers and commands used by official OpenAI Skills.

In my Windows workflows, MSYS-dependent commands fail under MXC while ordinary native PowerShell work continues. This breaks some Git operations and skill-directed command execution. Native `git.exe` can work while a shell/helper it launches fails; this is not a claim that all Git commands are broken.

The upstream issue is [microsoft/mxc#1061](https://github.com/microsoft/mxc/issues/1061). An upstream cause does not remove the need for Codex-level tracking, compatibility testing, and a supported way to complete the product's own workflows without weakening the sandbox.

## Upstream evidence

The upstream report includes a minimal Git Bash `bash.exe --version` reproduction: process creation succeeds, but MSYS initialization fails when accessing the Windows named-object namespace. The reported diagnostic is `NtCreateDirectoryObject(\BaseNamedObjects\...)` with access denied, followed by DLL initialization failure.

The [October 10 reproduction](https://github.com/microsoft/mxc/issues/1061#issuecomment-6097219833) reports the failure with BaseContainer/Tier 1 as well as the original AppContainer configuration. A [maintainer comment](https://github.com/microsoft/mxc/issues/1061#issuecomment-5669410665) says an attempted global-object ACL workaround did not succeed. The upstream issue remains open.

This is distinct from a normal filesystem-path permission denial or a request for broader Git network authorization. The upstream analysis concerns runtime initialization and named objects, not a project-directory allowlist.

## Local scope and limits

- Native Windows development workflows using Codex's MXC sandbox.
- Affected work includes MSYS-dependent Git shell/helper paths and commands used while following official OpenAI Skills.
- Native PowerShell commands continue to work.
- A separate Cygwin executable failure was also encountered, but its exact cause has not been independently established here; the concrete linked upstream reproductions use MSYS2/Git Bash.
- Current installed Codex/MXC versions, a sanitized local minimal reproduction, and the exact last-known-good version boundary have not yet been captured for this report. The upstream versions and diagnostics are not presented as measurements from my machine.
- Specific skill command traces are not attached; please include official Skills in compatibility coverage rather than treating a successful native shell launch as sufficient.

## Expected behavior

1. Standard Git workflows and commands prescribed by official OpenAI Skills should work within the active Windows sandbox, including their child processes and helpers.
2. If a toolchain path is incompatible with MXC, report that limitation accurately and provide a supported, policy-compliant execution path or actionable diagnostic.
3. Add regression coverage for MSYS-based commands and representative Git helper operations. Testing only PowerShell or `git.exe --version` misses this failure mode.
4. Track the upstream dependency and document affected configurations and the eventual supported fix.

Requiring unrestricted filesystem access or disabling isolation should not be the compatibility solution.

## Related reports

- [#15016](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/15016) covers an older Windows sandbox Git Bash signal-pipe failure. It is not proof that all MSYS failures share one cause.
- [#31073](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/31073) covers Git HTTPS/helper failures; [this comment](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/31073#issuecomment-6129366876) reports the same named-object symptom, without establishing the MXC backend.

This issue specifically requests Codex-level ownership of MXC toolchain compatibility and official Skills regression coverage. Please consolidate if that scope is already tracked.

## Summary

Dot-delegated tasks on my Windows computer do not use the restrictive local permissions profile I selected. They receive a separately managed `workspace-write` / `auto_review` policy, and the delegation interface provides no way to select my named profile or verify that its restrictions are preserved.

This is a least-privilege and privacy regression, not a request for Full Access. My intended policy denies filesystem access by default, allows writes in the project workspace, grants specific toolchain reads, and restricts command networking to an allowlist.

If delegation substitutes broader read access, private files outside the approved surface become available to a cloud-backed agent and may be transmitted to the hosted service when read, without the user being warned that their intended boundary was replaced. I am reporting that exposure risk; I am **not** claiming that private-data transfer or exfiltration has been observed.

## Observed workflow

- Native Windows computer, with a restrictive named local Codex permissions profile.
- Work is delegated from a ChatGPT dot to that computer.
- The delegated execution context reports a managed policy rather than the selected local profile.
- The dot task-creation interface does not expose a named-profile selector.
- Recent tasks used the intended project workspace. This is not a report that the project directory was accidentally replaced by a task directory on another drive.
- No supported method has been identified to make this delegation route retain and verify the intended restrictive policy.

Current Desktop and bundled-runtime version numbers have not been captured for this report. A fresh local diagnostic attempt is currently blocked by a task-resumption backend error; that error is not asserted to be the cause of the policy mismatch.

## Evidence limits

The observed problem is profile non-inheritance and lack of a supported, verifiable way to retain its boundary. The label `workspace-write` alone does not prove which individual read-deny or network rules are enforced. I have not performed a prohibited-read probe or collected private data to demonstrate the potential exposure. Effective launch overrides, configuration provenance, and network-proxy state still need to be verified.

The [permissions documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/permissions) describes named restrictive profiles and notes that legacy sandbox settings can supersede them. Please expose whether the dot launch route supplies such an override, rather than requiring users to infer enforcement from configuration text.

## Expected behavior

1. Honor the selected restrictive local profile for delegated tasks, including resumed turns.
2. If that profile cannot be enforced, fail closed before local execution and explain why.
3. Never silently replace a restrictive policy with a broader readable or network-accessible surface.
4. Show the effective profile and policy provenance, filesystem boundaries, command-network restrictions, and enforcing backend before execution.
5. Provide an explicit supported selection mechanism if dot tasks intentionally use independent policy.

Without a supported way to preserve this boundary, the only reliable mitigation available to me is to disallow local-running dot delegation entirely. Automated action review is not a substitute for deterministic filesystem and network limits.

## Related issue

[#50737](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/50737) reports dot launch-policy/default discrepancies, mostly from Full Access configurations or omitted writable roots. This report concerns the opposite security requirement: retaining a deliberately narrower boundary. Please consolidate if that restrictive-profile case is already tracked.

items.title: Windows: Browser/Computer Use crashes on start: trusted-worker.js gets NODE_REPL_TRUSTED_SERVICES undefined (trusted Node process exited unexpectedly / cua is not defined)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: mcp
labels.description: Issues related to the use of model context protocol (MCP) servers

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
## Summary

After the sandbox ACL fix (#51822) landed in CLI 0.163.0, the os error 32 setup failure from #51590 is gone (`setup refresh: ... errors=[]`). Browser Use still fails every time, in both the desktop app and the CLI:

- `trusted Node process exited unexpectedly; kernel reset, rerun your request`
- on retry: `cua is not defined`

The cause is visible in the MCP server stderr: `trusted-worker.js` gets no `NODE_REPL_TRUSTED_SERVICES` in its environment and throws on `JSON.parse`.

## Versions

- Windows 11 Pro, build 26300
- Codex CLI 0.163.0 (npm)
- Codex desktop (Microsoft Store) 26.1007.9446.0
- Bundled plugins `unified-computer-use` / `computer-use` / `browser` 26.1007.71326
- cua_node runtime `a9ba6825a525118c`, Node v24.21.0
- `[windows] sandbox = "elevated"` (same result with `unelevated`, see below)

## Stderr from the cua_repl MCP server (every attempt)

```
<anonymous_script>:1
undefined
^

SyntaxError: "undefined" is not valid JSON
    at JSON.parse (<anonymous>)
    at Object.<anonymous> (%TEMP%\.tmpIveTVU\trusted-worker.js:23:33)
    at Module._compile (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1929:14)
    ...
    at [eval]:63:24

Node.js v24.21.0
```

`trusted-worker.js` line 23:

```js
const configuredServices = JSON.parse(process.env.NODE_REPL_TRUSTED_SERVICES);
```

## Where the variable disappears

1. The plugin's `.mcp.json` (`unified-computer-use/26.1007.71326`) starts `cua_repl` (`node.exe ...@oai/cua-repl/bin/cua-repl.mjs`) with `"NODE_REPL_TRUSTED_SERVICES": "{\"browser\":\"@oai/browser-desktop/service\"}"` in `env`.
2. `@oai/cua-repl/dist/.../launch.js` spawns `node_repl.exe` with `env: { ...process.env, NODE_REPL_TRUSTED_SERVICES: process.env.NODE_REPL_TRUSTED_SERVICES ?? JSON.stringify(default), ... }`, so the variable is set at this point.
3. `node_repl.exe` launches `trusted-worker.js`, and the variable is undefined there.

So the variable is dropped inside `node_repl.exe` when it builds the trusted worker's environment. It never reaches the worker.

## Ruled out

- **Stale config paths:** all `node_repl` / `cua_repl` paths point to the current runtime and plugin version, and every file exists.
- **`shell_environment_policy`:** same crash with `-c "shell_environment_policy.include_only=[]"`.
- **Elevated sandbox:** same crash with `-c "windows.sandbox='unelevated'"`. The sandbox log confirms `Windows sandbox selection: unelevated`.
- **Desktop app vs. CLI:** both fail identically. They share the same cua_node runtime.

## Repro

1. Windows, desktop 26.1007.9446.0, CLI 0.163.0.
2. Start a fresh session and ask it to "test browser use on example.com".
3. The first browser action fails with "trusted Node process exited unexpectedly", and the retry fails with "cua is not defined". The stderr above appears in `~/.codex/logs_2.sqlite` under `codex_rmcp_client::stdio_server_launcher`.

Related: #51590 (sandbox ACL failure, now fixed by #51822). This report is the failure that remains after that fix.

The page has two radio choices, a number input and one button. Its click handler reads the selected choice/quantity, calls window.confirm with those values, then writes either an accepted result or a cancelled result to an output element. It prevents a second attempt. The page has no external requests or submission, with CSP connect-src 'none' and form-action 'none'.

Minimal shape of that handler (presentation/message simplified):

```html
<input type="radio" name="choice" value="A">
<input type="radio" name="choice" value="B" checked>
<input id="points" type="number" value="1000">
<button id="test">Open local confirmation</button>
<output id="result">pending</output>
<script>
let attempted = false;
document.querySelector('#test').onclick = () => {
  if (attempted) return;
  attempted = true;
  const choice = document.querySelector('input[name=choice]:checked').value;
  const points = document.querySelector('#points').value;
  const ok = window.confirm('Local test: ' + choice + ' / ' + points);
  document.querySelector('#result').textContent =
    ok ? 'accepted: ' + choice + ' / ' + points : 'cancelled';
  document.querySelector('#test').disabled = true;
};
</script>
```

Serve a self-contained page on localhost, then use the supported browser APIs.

## Chrome extension observations

1. Open a new extension-controlled tab at the local page.
2. Select B, fill 1000, and read the DOM. These succeed; the user confirmed the original foreground screen stayed unchanged.
3. Click the mock confirmation button once.
4. getJsDialog() returns type "confirm". A supported tab-scoped accessibility observation previously exposed the exact message plus Cancel and OK.
5. Calling the supported dialog.accept() times out:
   `Timed out after 10000ms waiting for CDP command Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled.`
6. A separate supported click targeting the observed OK button failed at the same focus-emulation command.
7. Ordinary tab close also failed while blocked. The user manually closed the local test tab; ordinary reads recovered.
8. Fully quitting/reopening Chrome produced a fresh extension connection. Normal site reads and local input worked, but one new dialog.accept() test reproduced the same timeout.

## Hidden in-app Browser comparison

1. Open the same local page through the official in-app Browser with visible:false.
2. Read visibility=false, select B, fill 1000, and read the DOM successfully.
3. Click the local confirmation button once.
4. getJsDialog() did not yield a usable confirm object (undefined). This does not establish that no modal existed.
5. A supported state read and then one ordinary close attempt failed with:
   `Timed out running CDP command "Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled" for tab 3`
6. No acceptance or completed output was verified. No additional confirmation attempts were made.

## Expected

The supported dialog API should discover the active modal, expose its message/origin, accept or dismiss that specific dialog, and permit the resulting page state to be read. Ordinary cleanup should remain possible. Please investigate whether a modal blocks focus/attachment initialization before dialog handling; that is an inference, not a source-level finding.

Please preserve URL, app permission and security checks; blanket dialog auto-acceptance is not requested.

## Scope and privacy

No installed runtime was inspected or patched, no direct CDP client or dialog interception was used, and no security settings were changed. All submission-like testing was local and synthetic. This report contains no real site/account data, private URLs, credentials, user filesystem paths, full session transcripts or personal screenshots.

For each case, is there a documented, bounded way to retrieve whether the event was eligible and dispatched, and whether the hook was trusted/enabled and completed, failed, or timed out? ### What issue are you seeing?

A PostgreSQL 17 build completed successfully during a Codex task running locally on macOS. Initializing a private, disposable test database intended for synthetic testing then failed. The planned database server startup and SQL tests were not reached.

The retained failure reports a small System V shared-memory allocation, shmget with size 56 bytes, failing with “Operation not permitted” (EPERM). The initialization command exited with status 1.

No production database was involved. The enforcement layer responsible for the denial has not been established, so this report does not attribute the failure specifically to Codex, macOS sandboxing, or a system resource limit.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

This is the observed workflow, not a confirmed minimal standalone reproduction:

1. Build PostgreSQL 17 successfully within a Codex task executing locally on macOS.
2. Run initdb to initialize a private, disposable database for synthetic tests.
3. Initialization fails at the small System V shared-memory allocation described above, before the planned server startup and SQL tests.

No fresh reproduction, permission-setting change, or restriction bypass was performed to prepare this report.

### What is the expected behavior?

Please clarify the supported local testing path:

1. Does the macOS local executor support the System V shared-memory allocation required by PostgreSQL initialization under its supported execution policies?

3. Is there a narrow, supported configuration for this local test workload, or is the workload unsupported in this execution environment?

If the operation is intentionally unsupported, an actionable diagnostic would help distinguish that from a PostgreSQL build or application-test failure.

### Additional information

PostgreSQL 17 documents that its default allocation uses both a small System V shared-memory segment and a larger anonymous mmap region. Using mmap therefore does not by itself establish that no System V allocation is needed:
https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/kernel-resources.html#SYSVIPC

Earlier runs using a binary with the same hash started successfully. However, equivalent effective permissions and execution conditions have not been demonstrated, so this is not a controlled regression claim.

The base64 payload in the UAC dialog decodes to:

```json
{"version":5,"offline_username":"CodexSandboxOffline","online_username":"CodexSandboxOnline","codex_home":"C:\Users\<user>\.codex","command_cwd":"C:\Users\<user>\.codex","read_roots":[],"write_roots":[],"deny_write_paths":[],"proxy_ports":[],"allow_local_binding":false,"oter_paths":[],"refresh_only":false,"hydrate_sandbox_users":false,"use_profile_root_policy":true}
```

Project threads load `network_proxy = true` and want ports `[3128, 8084]`. Daemon-internal threads run with cwd `~/.codex`, never load the project config, and want `[]`. Every alternation rewrites `setup_marker.json` and triggers another elevated setup. Concurrent setups also collide:

```
failed to grant non-inheriting read-attributes ACE on user profile C:\Users\<user>: open ACL target for root-only update: The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process. (os error 32)
Failed to create unified exec process: orchestrator_helper_incomplete: setup helper exited successfully before setup completed
```

The first upgrade from 0.160.0 to 0.162.1 caused the same storm (`sandbox setup marker missing or incompatible` plus the port change): 12 provisioning runs in about 60 s.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Windows 11, elevated sandbox, non-admin account.
2. Enable `[features] network_proxy = true` only in a project `.codex/config.toml`, not in `~/.codex/config.toml`.
3. Start or resume a thread in that project, ideally one with subagents, so the daemon also runs its own background threads.
4. Watch the UAC prompts and the `offline firewall settings changed` lines in the sandbox log.

Thread id: `01a141b9-8003-7cd1-a957-4d585234048d`.

### What is the expected behavior?

At most one elevated setup per real configuration change, and no oscillation between threads with different proxy settings. For example, the firewall rules could cover the union of the ports, or be keyed per proxy configuration. Parallel setup requests should also be serialized or deduplicated, so a single change produces one UAC prompt.

### Additional information

Workaround: remove `network_proxy` from the project config (or set it identically in the user config). Related: #40217, #30445 (setup helper / marker issues), #54440 (escalation ignored on the same machine).
